Player-facing narration addresses every player-controlled investigator in the second person of `play_language`.
When the grammar names the subject, use that language's natural second-person form; do not make the Keeper an
external camera that repeatedly calls the investigator by character name or third-person pronoun. Natural subject
omission is valid when the sentence still addresses the player. NPC dialogue and reported speech may address or
refer to the investigator as the fiction requires, and narration about NPCs remains ordinary third person. This
is semantic model judgment across an open language set, never a pronoun list, character-name regex or renderer
rewrite.

The production end is the base Keeper prompt. The prevention end remains the existing single tool-enabled
continuity audit, with no extra model call: every current context requires a checked
`player_address_review:{verdict:"pass"|"revise",quote:null|exact candidate excerpt}` beside
`intelligibility_review`. A revision quotes the narrator's third-person player reference, carries an actionable
finding to rewrite the whole candidate in second person without changing facts or choices, and forces the overall
review to revise. Missing, malformed or contradictory sub-reviews are artifact errors. The original candidate,
repair and reviewer artifact remain retained evidence.

The three ends (§31): the Keeper prompt writes the second-person narration; `narrate` and the player read it; the
checked pre-delivery reviewer prevents a drifted candidate from reaching either. Acceptance requires deterministic
producer/schema tests plus an original-save Web UI turn whose delivered narration addresses the same investigator
as `你`, with the retained audit artifact explicitly passing both intelligibility and player address.

## 121. Every spoken line is explicitly checked for intelligibility (2026-09-19, amends §120 and BUG-H73)

The first post-§120 wait turn still delivered `脉还在。气浅，眼没有` and `她这一床不睁`. The 1.2.27
reviewer submitted both required aggregate decisions in one request -- intelligibility pass and player-address pass
-- while the malformed words sat inside one well-formed `{{say:…}}` span. The rule already named clipped status
fragments and explicitly denied a terse-character exemption. The remaining failure was attention and evidence:
an aggregate null quote did not prove that the reviewer inspected each spoken line.

The existing review therefore gains one candidate-dependent checked object whenever the closed say-token syntax
contains speech: `speech_review:{verdict:"pass"|"revise",lines:[{quote,verdict}]}`. `lines` has exactly one row
per normalized say span, in text order, and `quote` copies that complete spoken text exactly. Artifact validation
derives the expected list deterministically from the product's closed say-token grammar; missing, reordered,
partial, duplicated or invented rows are format errors. Aggregate pass requires every line pass. Any line revise
requires aggregate speech revise, one actionable whole-candidate natural-language rewrite finding and overall
continuity revise.

This is not semantic classification in code: code recognizes only the product's closed machine-token boundary and
exact byte-for-byte coverage. The tool-enabled model still judges whether each quoted line is naturally
understandable in the open `play_language`, under §120's existing no-fragments rule. It adds no call, language
table, pronoun list, style score or minimum length, and NPC voice remains free once its sentence can be understood.

Acceptance: deterministic tests prove ordered exact coverage and contradictory aggregate refusal; an original-save
turn with NPC dialogue retains `speech_review.lines` for every say span and delivers natural, understandable speech.

**1.2.28 retained failure and 1.2.29 amendment.** Exact coverage alone exposed the miss but did not correct it:
the reviewer copied the complete line containing `这一床不睁` and still marked it pass. A bare verdict let the model
repeat the aggregate answer without articulating the grammatical joints it had actually checked. Each line row now
also requires bounded `reason`: for pass, why its subject/action/object or idiomatic omission is naturally clear;
for revise, which relation is missing or malformed. The host's final brief names scene-object/body-state metonymy
as a failure when it makes the reader reconstruct the person or action. Validation checks presence and bounds,
not the semantic answer.

The producer side also clarifies that retained delivered prose is continuity evidence, not a style or voice
authority. A Keeper may preserve facts and a person's register, but must not imitate malformed grammar merely
because the same character previously said it. This covers the raw recent dialogue that stays verbatim outside the
compressed capsule and was not reached by BUG-H73's original facts-not-phrasing sentence.


## 122. Typed Jev tasks and host-owned source references (2026-09-20)

Status: contract frozen for staged implementation; no hybrid product rollout is accepted.

Canonical design: [Jev unified runtime refactor](specs/jev-unified-runtime-refactor.md). The shared contract below is copied verbatim from that accepted design. S0 must prove the public SDK seam before dependent runtime/domain implementation; exact source references may proceed independently.

### Shared contracts

| Contract | Writer | Readers | Scoped fields and invariants |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IntentBinding | Host pins raw player input, chosen actor/goal/method/limits, turn/worldline/loop | Planner, dispatcher, admission | No LLM declaration is authorization; a resumed old plan must revalidate against the latest input |
| PlanPacket | Keeper role via checked private submission; host mints identity/version/dependency snapshot | Host validator, TaskRuntime | Semantic goal/subgoals/constraints, completion and evidence requirements, requested capabilities within allowed scope, replan/return conditions, optional derived-text request. Finite current intent; response may be a direct draft or need clarification. No opaque-ID echo, no full autonomous plot plan. Candidate actions come from host domains, not LLM-invented executable code |
| TaskContext | Host | TaskRuntime, domains, adapter | Host task/parent identity, owner, goal, scope/audience, read-set version bindings, remaining time/token/cost/action ceilings, checkpoint refs. Opaque handles host-only; semantic labels model-visible. Root/child real step sequence for replay |
| DecisionBatch | Domain caller | Adapter, Jev | Pinned model/family version/state/target aliases; independent Choice, Score, Noul questions whose instructions explicitly name the supplied state target or semantic alias; JSON question keys are correlation metadata, not inference input |
| DecisionResult | Adapter/Jev | Domain policy | Coverage, unknown/incomplete/reject/service-failure, raw scores, usage, latency. No free-form prose, code, URLs, fabricated IDs, or game-stat generation. Candidate args may select existing source values; host binds numeric, date, and record fields. No universal confidence cutoff and no confidence-as-truth |
| OperationProposal / ObservationPacket | Host builds proposal; execution writes observation | Dispatcher, TaskRuntime | Actual operation and host-bound args, basis refs, preconditions/read set. Result status/refusal/receipts/new refs/coverage comes only from actual execution. Source graphs and world are never modified by classification |
| SourceRef | Host | Resolver, consumers | Owner + document/record identity + revision + type + allowed field or half-open UTF-16 range, with context scope where applicable. Model sees semantic aliases/ordinals only. Exact strings preserved; no normalization, fuzzy re-anchor, or first-duplicate selection; surrogate splits forbidden. Existing recall code-point ranges are converted explicitly by the host. Normalization creates a derivative plus mapping. A SourceRef proves location and copy fidelity, not semantic truth, currentness, visibility, or visual proof. Originals for say/prose/records/numeric fields stay with the host. No every-name-to-opaque-ID migration. Historical reads remain readable; active job freshness is strict |
| TaskResult | Host | Owning tool interface, memory, delivery | Complete/partial/unresolved/needs_player/pending/failed/cancelled/stale internal outcomes mapped to existing owner interfaces. Original refs, used/omitted coverage, receipts, remaining needs. Not a new universal public response or schema dump. The writer receives real outcomes with audience and provenance, not unsupported promised actions |
| MemoryRecord | Host validated via existing memory submit | Capsule, recall, indexes | Source-ref-backed annotations and links plus an optional marked derived summary and a legacy-compatible read view. Module truth, recorded utterance, belief, and world receipt remain separate authority |

Missing, duplicate, unknown, stale, or incomplete required answers and invalid adverse references are not silently dropped. They produce the owning domain's incomplete/unavailable/refusal result. A numeric Score or Noul is decision telemetry, never a resource value or source-authored statistic.


### Implementation encoding decisions

The initial TypeScript encoding is `runtime/jev/contracts.ts`: SourceRef resource and revision are host-issued strings, scope loop is numeric, and sourceType is `turn | native_text | graph | record | draft`. PlanPacket wraps semantic `plan` with a versioned host envelope; it does not add host identifiers to model submission. PlanSubmission requires all eight semantic fields, no extra properties, at most 32 items per array, and 1–2048 UTF-16 units per semantic string; capability names are at most 128 units and must come from the host allowlist. At least one completion criterion is required. These are packet bounds, not semantic keyword rules.

Normalized DecisionAnswer uses `status: answered` plus a matching primitive and only that primitive’s fields, or `unknown | rejected`; service unavailability belongs to the batch outcome. Structural errors produce an incomplete result with every affected required question retained in coverage. Negative answers remain answered. Domain policy, not this binding function, interprets thresholds or refusal. Full optional Choice distributions must cover exactly the offered keys, sum to one within rounding tolerance, and contain finite probabilities. The API adapter owns raw-provider normalization.

### Failure and outage ownership

Failure is not global:

| Domain | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Source material publication/readiness | Error or review-unavailable remains not ready; no promotion, visual claim, or scanned-absence claim. |
| Narrative continuity review | A transport no-verdict may deliver explicitly unreviewed only under the incumbent contract; valid revise/unsupported/unavailable findings still refuse as that contract requires. |
| Post-delivery verifier | Advisory and never a delivery gate. |
| Workspace rerank/KIC | Deterministic original-order fallback within its existing 500 ms ceiling; shadow mode sends no remote request. |
| Admission | Fail closed. |
| RNG, world mutation, Git commit | Block the failed operation or delivery; retain all already-settled effects and receipts. |
| Required decision coverage | Owning domain returns incomplete/unavailable/refusal; missing answers are never dropped. |

Exact state, exact source, exact catalog/module/rule, secret-scope projection, and other sufficient local reads take the zero-Jev path. Jev is invoked only for a real semantic decision over host-issued candidates. Disabled or unconfigured Jev uses the declared incumbent or existing unavailable result; it never weakens admission.

### S0 private role protocol and integration gate

S0 is a bounded public-SDK seam probe, not S2's production TaskRuntime. The planner is a private lane of the configured Keeper role and receives exactly one private `submit_plan_packet` protocol tool for the strict semantic submission. That tool is not added to the normal global seven gameplay verbs, does not write player prose, and is not Workpad. A simple plan may instead return a direct draft through the private role response. The writer uses the existing `narrate`/`ask` role tools; there is no private `submit_delivery_draft` wrapper. Existing `message_end`, delivery-termination, and split-order guards remain authoritative. The writer receives only validated real observations. The host retains the complete private role transcript, typed artifacts, provider usage/accounting, read-dispatch trace, cancellation, audit evidence, and delivery result under existing privacy rules.

Before S0 can make a real guard claim, it extracts only the smallest shared read-dispatch seam from the incumbent path. That seam may share the existing schema validation, `tool_call` preflight, `runTool`, and `tool_result` failure accounting needed to route a guarded read. Its S0 capability set is limited to `look`, `recall`, and the explicitly classified read-only variants of `lookup`; a generic `lookup` label alone is insufficient. It has no mutation, preparation, publication, delivery, or raw `bridgeCall` bypass. The full CanonicalOperationDispatcher, all mutation families, and their parity/retirement work remain T05 and later. Passing S0 therefore proves the bounded real read path only, never full dispatcher or mutation conformance.

SDK mocks and test doubles may prove serialization, factory, subscription, and interface conformance only. They are explicitly not proof of provider auth, role delivery, model selection, Jev use, RPC behavior, guards, accounting, cancellation, or product acceptance. S0 passes only with a configured real Grok Keeper, real Jev typed endpoint, real host launcher and JSONL/RPC surface, and one guarded read-only objective requiring dependent Jev actions through the bounded shared read dispatcher above. The real trace must show the existing preflight and result-failure accounting; a test-double trace cannot substitute for it. The main session is the sole player; no fake Keeper or scripted-player acceptance is permitted.

New, resume, and fork each create/rebind the HostSessionAdapter, resubscribe to the correct events, and revalidate intent, scope, read set, deadlines, and owned work; no stale adapter, listener, checkpoint, or provider state crosses the boundary. The common caller deadline and cancellation must abort owned active work, distinguish awaiter yield from owner cancellation, and exclude late output. Provider/Jev/LLM/fallback tokens, cost, and context usage are attributed to the correct role and task without Grok misattribution. Secrets remain host-only (the bounded probe may receive a consuming-process environment binding) and are never persisted in session JSONL, prompts, artifacts, renderer settings, source, traces, or logs. The legacy launcher remains until all S0 checks pass; failure stops dependent hybrid rollout rather than introducing a private Pi patch, second RPC protocol, or dependency workaround.

### Dependencies, publication, ownership, and retirement

SourceRef may be developed and accepted standalone after contract freeze, without Jev or S0; hybrid use remains S0-gated. S1 freezes references, versions/read sets, outcomes, budgets, and dispatcher foundations. S2 requires S0+S1. S3 requires S2. Base S4 memory requires S1+S2 and is independent of PDF/S3. S5 ordinary resolve/apply requires S1+S2 and S3 only when new PDF material is genuinely needed. Promise end-to-end acceptance is the explicit S4+S5 join: S4 supplies promise evidence and S5 supplies canonical effect plus per-promise/per-instance fulfillment receipt; neither slice claims the join alone. S6 depends on S1+S2 and only the evidence/execution slices it consumes. KIC contracts #92-#98 and Keeper-pacing compatibility #99 are dependencies/references under their existing owners, not replacement planners; pacing adds no `progress debt`, `recovery_owed` gate, or second progress judge.

| Shared shape/path | Writer | Reader | Actor / publication or commit path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ScopeBinding | HostSessionAdapter/host | validator, runtime, domains, resolver | Host validates/narrows; no publication. |
| IntentBinding | Host from raw player input and current state | planner, admission, dispatcher | Host rebinds on input/resume; no model authorization. |
| PlanSubmission / PlanPacket | Keeper submits semantics; host validates and adds envelope | TaskRuntime, bounded replan/writer handoff | Runtime only; never directly commits. |
| TaskContext/checkpoint | Host TaskRuntime | domains, adapter, recovery | Runtime persists/revalidates; no world commit. |
| ReadBinding/read-set version | Owning host stores/runtime | validator, proposal gate, caches | Freshness gate before use/mutation. |
| DecisionBatch | Domain owner | DecisionAdapter and Jev | Adapter sends typed request; no execution. |
| DecisionResult | Jev through DecisionAdapter normalization | domain policy | Domain admits/refuses/selects proposal; no direct commit. |
| SourceRef | Host resource owner/resolver | evidence consumers, audits, memory | Source publication only through accepted source finish. |
| OperationProposal | Host domain/runtime | S0 bounded read dispatcher or, after T05, CanonicalOperationDispatcher | S0 invokes only classified read operations through incumbent guards; the full dispatcher alone invokes later accepted operations. |
| ObservationPacket | Dispatcher from actual result | TaskRuntime, replanner, writer | Receipts originate only in owning operation path. |
| TaskResult | Host TaskRuntime | owning tool, memory context, delivery | Mapped to existing owner interface; delivery remains guarded. |
| MemoryRecord | Post-commit host memory job through validated submit | capsule, recall, indexes, ledger | Memory submit publishes; derived indexes follow source order; no separate immediate Git commit. |
| Source graph/material | Accepted source owner | lookup, evidence, preparation consumers | Accepted source finish only. |
| World state/effect/receipt | TypeScript kernel | runtime, memory, delivery, replay | `resolve`/`apply`; atomic batch and stable call identity. |
| Draft/audit artifact | Keeper writer / existing reviewer | dispatcher, audit gate, retained evidence | `narrate`/`ask`, then existing audit and canonical Git commit. |
| Player delivery | Host after commit | player/session | Only after audit and canonical Git commit. |

Each slice must demonstrate its real producer, real reader, authorized actor, publication/commit route, legacy-reader compatibility, and rollback before cutover. Readers accept legacy and new accepted shapes before new writers are enabled. Cutover is per domain and attempt boundary, never mid-mutation. A replaced mandatory path retires only when its producer reaches a real consumer through the guarded path, acceptance passes, and routing can be disabled while accepted references, graph material, memories, receipts, effects, and Git history remain readable. Rollback disables routing; it never reverses committed player actions, rewrites Git, silently upgrades unsupported evidence, or deletes accepted data. Exact reads and standalone SourceRef remain usable with Jev off.

### S0 implementation decision: restricted recall through public hooks

The first probe is source-only, opt-in with `PI_COC_JEV_S0=1`, and restricted to a recent original-record question. It uses `createAgentSessionRuntime` plus `runRpcMode`. A factory creates the private role adapter for each replacement session. The original launcher is unchanged when the flag is absent. The probe does not support packaged deployment, setup, arbitrary CLI flags, writes, source preparation, or a general autonomous plot.

`runtime/jev/s0-read-dispatch.ts` calls the bound public Agent `beforeToolCall`, actual wrapped `recall` executor, and `afterToolCall`, using the same public argument preparation/validation and result override rules as Pi 0.85.1. This reaches both the kernel guards and all currently registered tool hooks. The parent is the real planner message; child operation identity is host-only. It deliberately emits separate `coc-jev-s0` trace entries instead of forging child assistant completions, Grok token usage, or Pi child tool-result messages. This proves a bounded hook-and-executor seam, not complete event/transcript or mutation parity. Full dispatcher extraction remains T05. Any relevant missing read-side consumer is a failed S0 gate, not permission to bypass it.

The probe selects a transcript scope, executes the listing, selects an issued original-page reference from that actual listing, executes it, and judges whether the resulting evidence satisfies the bounded plan. Missing evidence returns partial/unresolved. The first and second selection cannot share one request because the second candidate set does not exist before the first read. The final evidence judgment cannot precede the original-page read. The normal writer consumes the result through existing narrate/ask and all existing delivery guards. No user-visible operation or opaque child ID is copied through the plan.

The optional host task delivery guard is shared by explicit narrate/ask and canonical implicit narration. It checks the current task, deadline, and actual Keeper message identity before review and again immediately before the kernel delivery operation. With no guard installed the incumbent behavior is unchanged. A guard cannot authorize a delivery; all existing audits and kernel/Git rules still run. Already accepted kernel results remain authoritative. The S0 owner keeps its deadline active through composing, clears it on canonical commit/explicit ask success, and observes `coc:turn-committed` for implicit narration instead of guessing success from prose. This closes the same lifecycle boundary for both delivery routes.

### T04 lifecycle foundation decisions

Task leases own an absolute deadline, a cancellation signal, a captured scope, and remaining input/output token, cost, and action budgets. A child can only narrow capabilities and ceilings; its deadline never exceeds its parent's. Reservations charge the child and all ancestors atomically before work starts. Settlement releases unused reservation once; omitted actual usage conservatively keeps the reserved amount. A provider overrun remains accounted and cancels the affected root instead of silently granting more budget. Cancelling a child does not cancel its parent. A separately owned committed-memory root must carry its original turn and source references and never borrows the closed foreground lease.

Read-set comparison inspects only captured dependencies, so unrelated derived writes do not invalidate the whole task. Host-validated receipt advancement supplies expected old and actual new revisions; all old bindings are checked before any change is applied. It is not an authorization mechanism or a way for Jev to mint revisions. Checkpoints preserve the original deadline, remaining budget, step, scope, and settled receipts; they confer no replay permission. Owner outcome mapping is exhaustive over the internal outcome enum, with no universal fail-open/fail-closed default. An awaiter's yield ends only that wait, while owner cancellation aborts the owned task. Foundations remain unused by default until the production runtime ticket connects their real callers.

A checkpoint can be made only by an active lease. Resume additionally requires the owning runtime's explicit `authorizeResume` callback, which checks its current intent and durable revocation state; there is no permissive default. An old snapshot alone can never reactivate a cancelled task, including after a process restart. The generic lease does not invent a second task-status store. Both task-local and root-wide step counters survive checkpoint/resume. Committed-memory origins require full structurally valid SourceRefs, with exact scope, while the evidence owner remains responsible for resolving their recorded revisions.

The cancellation tree follows the established separation between [owner cancellation in Node](https://nodejs.org/api/globals.html#class-abortcontroller) and [nested cancellation scopes](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/cancellation). No new dependency or workflow service is introduced.

### T05 identity recovery and dispatcher decisions

An ambiguous mutation reply is reconciled before attempting a new operation. Host-only `table.call_status` reads the existing canonical `turn.calls` or retained turn record, using `campaign`, opaque `call_id`, and the exact prepared `request` (including its campaign/call_id). It compares the kernel's existing params digest and returns `settled` with the stored result or `absent` with the active turn/scope. A digest mismatch remains `idempotency_conflict`. An optional expected `{worldline, loop}` scope is checked against the active campaign; the dispatcher supplies its captured scope. This method performs no mutation, RNG, repair, source preparation, or new receipt and is not an eighth Keeper verb.

The task checkpoint owns operationId-to-kernelCallId, original proposal identity, and exact prepared payload bindings. Persist the binding before invocation. A matching settled result is evidence of previous execution and may be recovered even after the world advances; it does not authorize another write. An absent call from a different turn/scope is stale and must never be reinterpreted as a new current-turn operation. A still-unsettled same-turn operation must pass normal fresh guards before execution. The canonical kernel calls/receipts remain the only settlement store. Existing apply validates and accepts its effect batch as one semantic settlement; this is not a claim of filesystem atomicity across all append-only evidence files.

The dispatcher uses the public Pi `ExtensionRunner` call/result emitters and the registered COC definitions, so every existing tool hook participates without a fabricated child assistant message. The ordinary Pi handlers delegate to the same prepare/execute/finalize stages. Writer narration remains in the normal Pi message lifecycle. Host-selected operations have separate attempt identities for refusal accounting; they do not inflate Keeper provider-round counts. Source preparation is a separate capability, including when an otherwise read-only operation encounters material_pending. The bound campaign always overrides model input.

Unknown journal shapes are rejected. Currentness is revalidated after durable binding writes and immediately before invocation. A successful kernel settlement stays successful if later bookkeeping fails, with an explicit `bookkeeping_unavailable` diagnostic; it is never retried as a new effect. If a failed transport/post-hook path cannot establish whether a saved request settled, the result carries `settlement_unknown` and remains pending/cancelled until reconciliation. Cancellation after a known settlement retains the actual receipts and is reported separately from that settlement's outcome.

### T06/T07 decision port and API encoding

#### Shared Jev credentials (2026-09-21)

`extensions/jev` owns the single Jev credential setting, `ext.jev.apiKey`.
The PipiCOC settings section writes it through the existing `format: "secret"`
vault path; settings snapshots contain presence only. The host delivers
`EXT_JEV_APIKEY` privately when the enabled extension mounts. No credential is
written to campaign state, task checkpoints, argv, telemetry, or package assets.

All Jev consumers use this extension's `readJevApiKey(env)` resolver: the shared
decision adapter, source navigation, preselection, post-delivery verification,
S0 and local measurement tools. Source CLI runs may retain `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`
as a compatibility input to that resolver only. A managed App session never
falls back to an inherited CLI key when its extension is disabled, cleared, or
unconfigured. Explicit adapter keys remain available for isolated transport tests.

The settings UI is the writer, the shared resolver is the reader, and existing
decision callers are the actors. Saving a key does not enable any Jev domain or
change its existing fallback, deadline, budget, or gameplay authority. Existing
session restart boundaries refresh credentials. Preparation workers resolve the
same enabled extension's vault secret immediately before each spawn, so a cold
onboarding host also receives updates without serializing a key in its request.

The adapter keeps the pinned model and endpoint. The [TypeSafe API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api)
requires Bearer authentication; [VS Code secret storage](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-capabilities/common-capabilities)
confirms separating extension secrets from ordinary settings. Here the existing
PipiCOC vault remains the storage owner; no new credential store is introduced.

The runtime consumes `DecisionPort.decide(batch, lease) -> DecisionResult`. The adapter owns request packing, concurrency, retry policy and request usage reservations against that lease; the runtime must not debit the same API usage again. This interface is frozen before the two S2 modules are integrated. Transport implementation may proceed alongside TaskRuntime once T01/T02/T04 are accepted, but neither enables a new domain by itself and combined real-workflow acceptance remains required.

The official Score primitive uses 2–10 ordered `criteria` descriptors, not min/max request parameters. Its numeric range is 0 through criteria.length - 1, and its full legend/probability map must match those issued levels. The shared type now follows that encoding. Noul has a truth probability without a separate confidence field. Choice retains the offered-key map. Optional Noul true/false descriptors and structured criterion descriptors are preserved as JSON data. Raw telemetry never becomes a game statistic. Source: [official primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score). Production packing retains the master design's conservative policy rather than claiming a byte cap is a tokenizer count.

### T06 task loop and durable ownership

Registered domain policies produce either an exact host operation, one same-state decision batch, a terminal result, a source wait, or a bounded replan request. A policy receives actual prior observations and decisions; it never supplies a generated script. The runtime owns identities, phase transitions, operation journals, a finite step ceiling and cancellation. The canonical dispatcher remains the only gameplay operation executor; background memory may use only explicitly registered owner publication ports and cannot deliver narration or commit a foreground turn.

One task record stores the plan revision, original intent, lease checkpoint, ordered decisions/observations, pending operation proposal and identity journal. It is coordination metadata, not another world/receipt ledger. The exact pending proposal survives a restart and is reconciled through the canonical dispatcher. Duplicate completed operation keys do not execute again. A decision in flight is checkpointed with its remaining token/cost allowance conservatively unavailable; only a returned, accounted result restores the actual remainder. A crash cannot refund unknown provider usage. Resume requires the latest durable record, explicit owner authorization of current intent/scope, the original deadline and a current dependency read set. Cancellation records a durable terminal status; an earlier copied checkpoint cannot supersede it.

Foreground cancellation and session shutdown abort owned leases immediately, then persist revocation in order. An independently committed memory root survives a later player input; shutdown retains its pending work for owner-authorized resume. Ready foreground tasks retain their deadline through the ordinary writer's audit/commit/delivery. Simple direct drafts enter that same guarded writer path without a Jev call. A genuine decision boundary returns needs_player; absence of a boundary never fabricates a question.

The host-only `_context` includes `world_revision`, a digest over current world, party, receipts and pending choice, for current-task revalidation. Turn state bookkeeping alone does not change this dependency. The additive field does not alter the default-off Keeper context policy. The optional delivery guard may be asynchronous: exact/direct composition and currentness are durably checked before the existing audit and again before invocation. No guard result skips a domain audit.

The first S2 integration domain is explicitly bounded `table-evidence`: read-only look/recall and actual issued continuation objects. It does not claim the later broad source, memory, or mutation domains. Its typed next-action and independent per-requirement support questions share the same actual evidence snapshot. The 0.95 support gate is a conservative family policy requiring real acceptance, not a calibrated accuracy claim. The source-mode `PI_COC_TASK_RUNTIME=1` route replaces the S0 loop for this opt-in domain; the S0 flag remains only as a historical probe.

T06 recovery hardening: task files use the existing native descriptor lock plus monotonically checked replacement, so an old writer cannot supersede a newer revocation or reservation. Closed cancellation permits only `reconcileCancelled` over the saved proposal/request; a settled receipt is retained and an absent result is recorded without a write. Gameplay authority stays closed. Session shutdown fences late task publications, retaining independently committed memory work for its existing memory owner to discover and rebase in T09. Expired checkpoints are never given a new deadline. Structural task-record validation precedes owner authorization. The owner-facing completion method requires accepted canonical narration commit evidence or an accepted mechanics-choice identity after the audit/commit guard phases; commit failure can return to audit for an existing bounded repair.

Pi's earlier input hook may hold a non-resend player input before later extension hooks run. The kernel now emits `coc:player-input-queued` at that existing queue boundary; an installed task owner cancels obsolete foreground work immediately and binds the replacement only when the original input is replayed. Resend holding and default behavior without a task owner remain unchanged. Keeper provider requests reserve input/output/cost/action allowance before dispatch, using conservative payload bytes, the configured output ceiling and model cost metadata; returned usage settles the reservation. Unknown/error attempts keep their reservation. Jev has its separate provider accounting through the same root lease.

Owned registration is a real write even when it only enriches equipment already carried. When task receipt tracking is enabled, deferred Mod registration requests `_task_read_set: true` on its existing table.apply call. The TS apply transaction returns `_task_advance` with the exact before/after world revision, original turn/worldline/loop, call identity and actual receipt IDs. These are captured within that operation, not by two racy surrounding reads. The Mod owner forwards that accepted result to `coc:task-receipt-advance`; the active task can advance only when its captured old revision and scope match. The event cannot execute or authorize a write. Foreign changes still invalidate the task. Without task tracking, the existing request/response shape remains unchanged.

T06 required #99 compatibility (keeper-pacing specification D4): retire the Director `recovery.owed/takes/steps` producer and the host's first-narrate `recovery_owed` refusal, including when an old capsule contains those fields. Quiet clarification, informed refusal and an already completed goal require no new receipt. Existing obstacle counts, Director scores/offers and adoption telemetry remain advisory and remain implemented. The no-tool implicit-delivery correction routes to ordinary delivery; it cannot demand a new event or effect. This is the core compatibility slice only; versioned Mod instruction alignment and the separately specified pacing A/B acceptance are not claimed here.

Pinned Jev live wire evidence shows full Choice probability maps rounded to hundredths whose reported sum can be 0.99. Shared probability validation now accepts an exact sum within its original tolerance, or a cent-grid map whose per-value rounding intervals collectively contain total mass 1. Missing/extra candidates, nonfinite/out-of-range values and impossible mass still fail. Raw probabilities and confidence are retained without renormalization. This handles representation precision, not semantic uncertainty or confidence calibration.

Table-evidence family v2 replaces the uncalibrated 0.95 Noul completion gate with explicit per-requirement Choice coverage (`sufficient`, `needs_more`, `unavailable`). Live v1 read exact sheet fields but still labelled all requirements missing, then returned partial while its next-action answer said complete. In v2, a global completion cannot override missing evidence: the host follows the best positively weighted remaining issued read candidate, still subject to ordinary scope, uniqueness and step limits. An original-page requirement cannot be satisfied by a card head. This is domain control flow over actual candidates, not a universal probability cutoff. Old v1 task records retain their original family version and cannot silently resume as v2.

### T08 native text snapshot boundary

The host source owner adds `sourceText(pdf,{pages,expected_file_sha256?},signal)`, using unique 1-based physical pages (1–32 per request). It returns the bound PDF SHA, `pdfjs-<version>:native-text-v1`, page count, exact native snapshots in requested order and explicit per-page extraction errors. A snapshot contains page, PDF label, raw deterministic PDF.js text, UTF-8 text SHA, availability text/empty and a revision digest of `[extractionVersion,fileSha,page,textSha]`. No text normalization, OCR, fabricated empty page, image observation, support or readiness is implied. Empty text is not evidence of absent content. Source stamp/expected SHA and cancellation are checked by the same PDF owner; shared extraction never destroys a peer's document lease.

Native SourceRef resource names are host-only `pdf:<fileSha>:page:<physicalPage>:native:<extractionVersion>`, revisions are snapshot.revision, and UTF-16 selectors point into the exact snapshot text. Scope/audience is issued by the active source owner. This helper alone produces no SourceProof or publication. The domain owns bounded span formation/coverage, native-extractive consultation eligibility and fallback to the existing original-page author/reviewer/finish path. Durable native cache bytes remain source-derived snapshots, never another readiness ledger.

### T09 committed-turn reference catalog boundary

The memory owner supplies the original committed turn, actual commit, exact player_text and rendered Keeper text with its original campaign/worldline/loop and stable campaign owner scope. The pure host catalog emits whole-role immutable SourceSnapshots and ordered exact segments: resource `turn:<turn>:player|keeper`, revision SHA-256 of the complete exact role text, UTF-16 half-open selectors and host-issued role/ordinal aliases. The actual commit remains separately checked by the memory job at both intake and publication; matching text alone never proves a committed origin.

Closed syntax segmentation prefers paragraph/newline and sentence punctuation boundaries within an 800-code-unit ceiling, never splits a surrogate pair, and does not trim/normalize any original character. Every code unit belongs to one segment; joining them recreates each whole role. Duplicate equal occurrences keep separate refs. Empty roles are explicit. There is no twelve-segment cap. This catalog cannot classify, publish, mint a world fact or decide memory relationships. T09's kernel-owned batch cursor, explicit links, validated original context and committed-memory TaskRuntime owner remain required before replacing the incumbent extraction lane.

Shared scalar/ScopeBinding/SourceRef values, ContractError and plain-record validation live in the provider-free `runtime/jev/value-contracts.ts`; the public contracts module re-exports them unchanged. The exact SourceRef resolver imports only that pure module. Kernel admission can therefore reuse the same reference validation/extraction without importing Pi, TypeBox tool schemas, PDF handling or a second implementation.

Committed-turn segmentation emits each complete syntactic sentence/newline boundary even below 800 units; the ceiling is a safety fallback, not a reason to merge many statements. Closing punctuation/quotes and trailing original whitespace stay with the preceding segment, decimal dots between digits are not boundaries, and unpunctuated long runs remain surrogate/CRLF-safe chunks. This creates distinct selectable short occurrences while preserving complete exact concatenation.

Independent source/memory decision groups may freeze up to sixteen complete batch inputs before dispatch. Their requests share the captured task scope/read set and adapter concurrency/budget controls; no question can read a peer result. The runtime counts each batch against the same step/action allowance and preserves all typed results before taking a dependent step. A group exceeding the remaining allowance returns explicit partial coverage rather than dropping batches. Pending provider usage is conservatively checkpointed before any request. This is fan-out within the same TaskRuntime, not a second loop.

### Registered owner operations

The canonical dispatcher may register a private typed owner operation for PDF/native reads or memory/source publication. These are not extra Keeper verbs or fabricated Pi tool calls. The registration fixes capability, read/publication kind, argument validator and the existing owner's executor; models cannot register operations or supply executors. Shared task/scope/read-set/budget/journal guards run before invocation. Gameplay verbs still traverse the complete public Pi hook/prepare/execute/finalize path. Source and memory publication keep their own kernel-validated job/step/lease replay authority; a dispatcher registration never makes arbitrary RPC or file writes legal. Read-only nested owner work does not wait behind its enclosing gameplay tool, avoiding a parent/child dispatch deadlock.

`module.source.snapshot` is a host-only read of the active library/campaign source binding, available before graph identity exists. It returns the registered original PDF path/SHA/page count and a metadata generation revision without claiming readiness or opening the PDF in the kernel. The host verifies the expected bytes before native extraction. Its raw paths and hashes remain inside the source task; the Writer receives semantic result data and public page labels, while full refs/read sets stay in host details.

An exact ordinary Pi read may bind the active task lease before execution without a Jev decision. `bindReadScope` accepts only the closed read capabilities, charges one action/step and installs the same frame checked by kernel invocation and source-preparation capability gates. It does not fabricate an assistant/tool call or grant publication. A local lookup that later needs source preparation cannot silently exceed its captured read capability. The normal public Pi result/delivery lifecycle still owns that call.

Task source dependencies use an additional host-only `task_source_revision`: the same graph/generation/configuration inputs as the existing context binding, excluding the module's operational `reading` job/cache ledger. A checked consultation cache write does not change authored facts or readiness and must not invalidate its own waiting task. Actual graph/generation/source/configuration changes still invalidate it. The existing `source_revision` and KIC policy remain unchanged; consumers without the new field use their existing revision. This separates task dependencies from reader bookkeeping without ignoring accepted source changes.

A host-only `module.source.answer.peek` reads a matching accepted visual consultation without creating or claiming a job. It validates the original source/generation, reads the retained draft/review bytes against their accepted digests, and materializes the answer from the checked draft bytes rather than trusting a duplicate answer string in cache metadata. It returns a host evidence descriptor for exact reference to that accepted derived answer. Cache misses remain misses, not queued work; no model or publication occurs.

### T09 referenced memory publication

`memory.job {campaign,turn?,mode:"referenced"}` uses the existing extraction job/backlog owner. A new referenced job verifies the committed Git turn and campaign metadata, compares the current retained original texts, and captures the original worldline/loop. The active scope must still match at publication. The existing non-referenced protocol and completed legacy jobs remain readable; an already-started legacy job is not silently converted.

The packet has `protocol:"memory-reference-v1"`, `job_id`, `turn`, `commit`, `origin:{scope,revision}`, `step:{key,sequence,total,remaining,segments}`, `known_entities`, `prior`, `story_context?`, and `story_sources`. Segments are `{alias,role,text,ref}` from the exact catalog, at most twelve per step, with no whole-job segment cap. `prior` supplies occurrence-specific `{alias,kind,subject,statement,status}` from earlier same-scope candidates. Opaque ids, commits, refs, step keys and revision bindings are host metadata and are excluded from model prompts. The model sees semantic names, issued ordinal aliases and original text only. Target enumeration coverage is explicit; a bounded prior pool cannot establish absence of all older claims.

`memory.submit {campaign,job_id,referenced:{step,decisions,story?}}` accepts exactly one decision for every currently issued segment, in source order. A decision is `{source:alias,outcome:"retain"|"skip"|"defer",annotations?}`. Retain requires one to eight annotations, with unique kinds from the existing eight-kind enum. Each annotation has `kind,subject,knowers?,entities?,privacy?,state?,confidence?,relations?`; it has no statement or source coordinates. The kernel materializes exact statement text and refs from the issued segment. Relations are `{relation:"duplicate"|"reinforcement"|"independent"|"correction"|"contradiction"|"temporal_change",target:priorAlias}`. Correction requires keeper_correction; correction and temporal_change close only the explicitly selected older occurrence. Independent promises never supersede solely by subject/entities. Other links retain both records. Published rows preserve the existing statement view plus `memory_version:2`, `statement_ref`, `source_refs`, and typed `relations` bound to actual record ids.

Story assessments use the existing status/thread/bridge fields with `frame_source` and `delivery_source` aliases instead of copied text. Non-unclear frames must select a player segment; a delivered bridge selects a Keeper segment. The existing acquired-causal-evidence checks still apply. The kernel stores exact resolved legacy views with their refs. A job with story context cannot finish without an assessment; missing semantic answers remain deferred.

Every submission binds the kernel-issued step key. Before publishing, the same job stores a prepared step with digest, allocated candidate identities and exact derived rows. Recovery merges that prepared step idempotently, repairs the NPC ledger/story/event projections, then advances the cursor and records the result. Changed replay fails. A deferred segment stays in durable job/backlog state, and later source-order steps continue; after the first pass, a fresh owner dispatch can retry deferred segments. Completion requires every segment resolved and any required story assessment. No thirteenth segment is dropped, no pre-commit job is admitted, and no memory publication grants a world effect or reward.

Host-only `memory.source {campaign,turn}` revalidates the original commit/text/scope and returns its origin binding without opening, recovering or publishing a job. Committed-memory tasks use that immutable binding, not the changing foreground turn/world revision. Only the registered `memory-write` domain under owner `memory` may invoke `memory.job`/`memory.submit` with `memory.write` on a committed-memory root; background resolve/apply/narrate/ask remain prohibited. The existing lane queue initiates these tasks after commit and retains its scheduling/shutdown behavior.

Referenced default dispatch may revisit referenced pending/backlog jobs on a new session. Host-only `exclude_turns` (at most 128) prevents the same session's backfill allowance from repeatedly consuming the same uncertain job; the existing queue still limits total backfill attempts. Legacy pending jobs retain their prior explicit-retry policy. No exclusion deletes history or marks a job complete.

Concurrent decision admission acquires its transport slot before reserving the bounded provider spend. A queued budget reservation may wait only while existing reservations could release enough allowance at every ancestor; genuine total insufficiency refuses before fetch. Settlement wakes bounded waiters, and the original abort/deadline cancels waiting. This avoids mistaking several queued worst-case holds for actual spent usage while preserving the same ceilings and conservative unknown-attempt charge.

### Typed task view dependencies

The broad `world_revision` stays unchanged for existing context/audit/KIC readers. The kernel additionally produces `task_world_revision` and `task_presentation_revisions`. A closed kernel owner registry partitions only declared derived presentation fields; the first owner is the NPC voice lane's lines-shaped `voice_mask`, `exchanges`, and retired `sample_lines`. The voice writer and revision partition share the same owner field declaration. Unrecognized fields, wrong owner/shape, other Mod state, inventory, party, clocks, receipts, pending choices and all gameplay state stay in the core world binding.

Read-only evidence/source tasks bind `task_world_revision` (falling back to broad world_revision for older hosts) and the existing source/family/model bindings. They do not consume newly generated voice presentation. Voice-consuming draft/review/cache families retain their broad binding or explicitly bind the supplied presentation revision; this change does not weaken those incumbent audits. An actual ordinary apply receipt optionally carries both broad and task before/after bindings so the corresponding active task advances the correct revision. No receipt is fabricated for a voice job, and no generic foreign background write receives advancement authority.

Committed memory also preserves the speech attribution already encoded by `say`. The kernel derives rendered UTF-16 speech boundaries from the committed repaired marked text and its ordered canonical speech rows, through the same marker removal/space-collapse/trim transform. It never searches for a copied substring. Equal spoken occurrences retain their own boundaries and speakers. A segment carries host-issued `attribution:{kind:player|keeper_narration|speech|mixed|unknown,speaker?:{name,kind:npc|investigator|label}}`; malformed or unavailable original mapping remains unknown. Player statements, NPC speech, mixed or unknown segments cannot be published as unqualified world_event. They remain attributed reports, beliefs, promises or explicit deferred work. This enrichment does not re-anchor or change existing text SourceRefs.

Every statement-bearing memory projection uses the shared closed semantic evidence view: recall/capsule, continuity hypotheses/corrections, promise obligations/NPC history, continuity audit and cross-loop recall retain `authority:conversation_report` and the available attribution. Missing/malformed attribution on a version-2 row becomes explicit unknown; the projection does not expose opaque speaker identities. Prepared-step recovery requires equality of the complete already-present candidate row, not just its text/ref. A differing semantic payload refuses before secondary views or job completion, preserving the conflict for recovery rather than publishing divergent readers.

Verified canonical speech speakers extend the referenced job's issued name catalog even when they are offstage. A table-assigned speaker name binds host-side to its already resolved NPC/investigator identity; the model never translates aliases into ids. Unresolved labels do not become entities. Multiple issued names for the same resolved identity collapse only after deterministic binding, preserving the single-entity relationship constraint without duplicate knower/entity rows.

### Fresh source navigation assist

An optional `fresh-source-navigation/2` TaskRuntime domain runs for the first fresh skeleton attempt, after canonical source binding and before its tool-enabled visual author. It binds the claimed original PDF to `module.source.snapshot` before any graph exists, reads native text through the existing host source owner, and classifies bounded issued parts with independent closed page-role decisions. Roles are `contents`, `opening`, `global_background`, `scene`, `npc`, `monster`, `parameters`, `plot`, `rule`, `map`, `handout`, `cross_reference`, and `other`; every role decision is yes/no/uncertain, and a page may have several roles. Neither page roles nor a parameters hint supply playable parameters. Version 2 pins explicit role definitions in each immutable batch state: usable game statistics count as parameters without that literal word, NPC and monster content may overlap, an authored opening is distinct from an ordinary arrival, and a contents/reference pointer is distinct from the content it points to. Version-1 navigation is retained as historical quality evidence and is not reused by version 2.

The host materializes `{version:1,navigation_only:true,source_revision,extraction_version,page_count,hints:[{page,pdf_label,roles}],coverage:{classified_pages,uncertain_pages,empty_pages,error_pages,omitted_pages}}`. Pages and roles are host-bound selections, never generated numbers or names. Empty/error/garbled native text stays unknown rather than proving absence. Whole-document coverage is explicit; a budget/deadline/step limit keeps useful partial hints alongside omitted/uncertain pages. The task returns no SourceProof, graph node, material-ready assertion, visual observation or publication.

The one shared composition supplies an optional navigator callback to ReadingService in onboarding and module preparation. `task.navigation_hints` exposes only semantic hints and coverage to the existing reader, excluding source hashes/refs/task identities. Navigation task records and reusable artifacts stay in the host-owned task-runtime directory outside the tool-enabled reader cwd, bound to the module, reading job, source, extraction version and decision family. A same-job retry may reuse that artifact after current source/native-probe validation. Only sanitized hints enter task.json. Existing skeleton(opening candidates, empty ready_nodes) and selected-opening author/reviewer/finish behavior remains authoritative. Original pages must still be opened and independently reviewed before `module.read.finish`; typed hints do not enter read_pages or review_pages. Unavailable, stale or disabled navigation uses the existing visual navigation path. It does not block preparation or require a completed whole-book index. Setup keeps its existing host and never masquerades as a public Keeper play session.

The canonical dispatcher can be composed with registered owner operations alone, without a Keeper AgentSession or gameplay stages. This composition still validates capabilities, identity journals, scope, read sets, budget and cancellation. Ordinary gameplay operations require their actual public Pi session and stages and otherwise refuse; no fake session, assistant/tool call, or replacement hook path is supplied for setup navigation.

A registered owner domain can declare artifact completion. Its finished foreground task closes after producing its owner artifact instead of entering the Keeper writer phase; shutdown preserves that terminal result. This declaration does not provide gameplay/delivery authority. Table-evidence foreground tasks still require ordinary guarded writer delivery and canonical commit; committed-memory roots retain their existing independent completion behavior.

### T10 adaptive memory read

The existing `recall` verb gains optional `query` for `what:memory`. A query cannot be combined with direct `read` or `detail`; no-query behavior and its bounded continuations remain unchanged. Query reads remain Keeper-private conversation evidence and never settle a promise, change memory or grant player/NPC knowledge. If the typed host is unavailable, the query is explicitly unavailable with the ordinary direct-read fallback; it is never silently ignored.

The kernel memory evidence owner provides a bounded, disposable query snapshot over the requested authorized line/turn/name/kind filters. It includes the whole eligible candidate pool rather than only recent/current-NPC hits, preserves occurrence-specific identity/attribution/relations, and supplies complete source-order raw segments for extraction gaps. Raw fallback can widen to all retained committed history if indexed evidence is insufficient. Candidate aliases and cursors are issued by the host; opaque snapshot/commit/ref bindings are excluded from decision prompts. Snapshot navigation is not proof of semantic truth.

The private owner operations are snapshot, page, original read and finish. Pages are at most 20 rows and 12 KiB including metadata. An original read resolves a selected occurrence against the canonical Git turn, preserves exact Unicode text and speech attribution, and returns bounded surrounding context plus explicit continuation/omission data. Legacy generated statements remain marked derived reports; they are never re-anchored by substring matching. A query-scoped SourceRef is newly issued for its verified original resource under the caller's authorized read scope; existing stored SourceRefs remain unchanged, and original worldline/loop/commit provenance travels separately.

The TaskRuntime memory-read domain scans independent candidates in batches, reads actual originals as necessary, and then judges relevance, support for the requested question, present applicability and contradiction over the returned evidence. Later judgments see actual prior observations, never simultaneous peer answers. Indexed rows, raw gaps and any later raw widening have separate used/omitted/unknown coverage. A missing or abbreviated antecedent such as a promise's condition requires original context, not a guessed reward rule. Unknowns remain explicit. The final result is at most 20 rows/12 KiB; omitted evidence does not become a completeness claim, and exact original continuations remain available through the existing owner.

Query snapshots are read-only, bounded host/kernel caches, not a second memory truth store or queue. Source/index changes are detected at finish; the same domain may refresh and re-evaluate within the original caller's deadline/budget, otherwise it returns partial/stale coverage. World, scope and consent dependencies still pass the canonical dispatcher and final delivery guards. Existing direct recall and retained raw Git history remain the rollback path.

### T11 ordinary resolve routing

The opt-in ordinary resolve domain uses a read-only `table.resolve.options {campaign}` snapshot. Its `context._binding` carries `{campaign, worldline, loop, turn}` — the state the snapshot was read at, which the host's check-preflight (§124) and the ordinary resolve domain use to bind a decision to it; readers that do not bind strip it, and it is never offered to a model. The kernel emits the current investigator skill/characteristic vocabulary and canonical bound availability from SkillResolver, plus compiled rule decision names/families and current pending choice/session. Missing bindings stay unavailable, including specialized healing parameters; a classifier cannot fill them. The host exposes semantic profile aliases, never numeric arguments to generate. Closed choices select an actor/skill, ordinary family, difficulty and dice modifier from the actual current snapshot; independent intent/uncertainty/consent judgments must agree before a single ordinary check is proposed. An absent need to roll completes with no mutation; unsupported families and genuine player choices stay with their incumbent owner.

The host constructs `resolve` from the selected issued profile and original declared goal/method; the canonical public dispatcher still runs admission, Mod preflight, schema checks and the existing kernel transaction. Jev grants no authorization. The runtime persists one operation identity and exact request before invoke; a lost response queries `table.call_status` and reuses that identity, never a new roll. A real settled receipt advances only the executing task and its ancestors to the new world/party/receipt revision. Cancellation after settlement preserves that receipt. A same-goal continuation never creates progress debt or an extra mandatory action.

Precedent cross-check: [AWS idempotent APIs](https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/) and [Stripe idempotent requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests) both support stable caller identity and parameter consistency across retries. The local kernel remains authoritative: those precedents do not establish atomicity, consent or replay correctness here; the existing canonical call record and actual RPC tests must prove them.

### T14 selected family: post-delivery verification

`post-delivery-verifier/1` is the first closed T14 family. It retains exactly the six incumbent advisory finding kinds and the existing post-commit scheduling, `table.warn`, one-turn capsule and unrecorded-clue consumers. The host enumerates exact delivered-source spans and fact/clue aliases; Jev selects only issued aliases and closed verdicts. The host resolves quotations and canonical clue names without model copying, and supplies the existing reader's bounded English explanation. Original positions, commit identifiers, private credentials and source bindings remain host-side. Syntax segmentation provides ranges only and never classifies open semantics.

A family attempt pins routing before its first call. Incomplete, unavailable, malformed, stale or exhausted Jev evaluation is explicit and may run the incumbent verifier once under that attempt's original deadline/budget. No clean verdict is inferred from missing answers. Only one route publishes warnings. The family remains advisory after commit: no blocking, reopening, world effect, player question or progress obligation, and no added foreground planner. Empty receipts, quiet dialogue, refusal and goal completion are not warning kinds. Disabled routing uses the incumbent. Enabling the experimental route is not retirement: paired quality and whole-slice cost/latency gates must pass before the prior mandatory call retires.

T10 memory-read policy version 4 ranks every relevant occurrence with an independent closed query-specific priority judgment before canonical original reads. Full issued text reaches both relevance and priority; no answer-bearing tail is clipped into a navigation head. Priority is essential/useful/unknown/background, with stable order within a class; it is not a recency, name or kind heuristic. This order also governs the bounded final evidence packet. Every unselected or transport-omitted occurrence remains explicitly unknown/omitted. Snapshot refresh invalidates prior relevance and priority judgments even when aliases repeat. Oversized context/comparison inputs preserve explicit omission metadata and unknown assessments, while already verified useful evidence still reaches finish. A recall-only parent adopts its completed memory-owner outcome instead of launching a redundant whole-observation judgment that can exceed the provider input bound.

Invalid domain decision data is rejected before transport and before appending it to a durable task record. This prevents undefined mixed-source fields or a malformed decision result from poisoning the record and stranding an otherwise completed child. A failed artifact closes with an explicit reason; storage failure still aborts authority rather than silently rebuilding the coordination record.

Version 5 preserves the planner's separate semantic subquestions across the memory owner seam (`memory.search.needs`, host-only). The child uses those needs as evidence requirements; a public single-question recall falls back to its original query. Each full occurrence is independently classified against each need as essential/useful/background/irrelevant/unknown. Host selection alternates among these per-need buckets, deduplicates aliases, and only then applies read/result bounds. This prevents a repeated topic from filling the result before another requested topic is considered. Original-source verification, support/applicability/contradiction judgments and explicit omitted coverage still follow. No priority or semantic classification grants truth, public knowledge, player consent or a reward.

### T14 audit source-selector compatibility

> **Amended by §130.8 (2026-09-23).** Subreviews live inside `continuity_review`; one shared sentence states it to the reviewer, and a subreview submitted beside `continuity_review` is moved into place rather than refused.

The next closed family is `audit.continuity.v2`, activated only by a newly versioned narration-audit package. It keeps the existing tool-enabled reviewer, review count, semantic predicates, repair allowance and delivery gate. The kernel pins an occurrence catalog over the candidate draft, current player input, ordered normalized say spans, allowed retained evidence strings, offered objects/scenes and causal-reentry evidence. Model-visible entries carry only semantic aliases and exact values. Private SourceRefs bind their original field/range, scope and revision; aliases never re-anchor by substring search.

A v2 reviewer selects `claim_source`, `evidence_sources`, `source`, `claim_sources`, `locus_source`, `evidence_source` and `missing[].subject` instead of copying claims, evidence quotes, every spoken line, scene names, clue/relation pairs or object names. Speech selection must cover each issued occurrence exactly once in its original order. Generated reasons, findings, fixes and summaries remain reviewer-owned. A v2 alias is mutually exclusive with its v1 copied field; missing/foreign/wrong-family/reordered/duplicate/stale selections refuse as targeted format errors. No adverse review is discarded or converted to pass.

The owning kernel resolves v2 selections into the existing canonical v1-shaped accepted artifact before the current consistency validator and delivery actor run. The raw selector artifact is retained separately under the pinned v2 job. Both v1 and v2 capabilities are advertised; v1 locked packages and retained artifacts stay readable without rewriting. The next narration-audit package is 1.2.30 with the v2 requirement and unchanged state version; activation follows the existing safe package boundary. Package digests and the pinned request keep approval caches distinct. Targeted evidence reads return stable issued aliases with their bounded values. This migration adds no model call and claims copy fidelity only until real semantic acceptance passes.

### T12 bounded apply and finite fulfillment terms

The first ordinary apply catalog contains host-issued effects already grounded in current source/state: registered movement and reachable clue delivery, followed by finite cash/item/object fulfillment when all terms have their own source binding. The host never treats a relevance score as authority or fills a missing amount/profile with zero. One selected effect batch uses the existing public apply schema, admission, Mod preparation, kernel staging, call journal and canonical receipts. Unsupported effect families remain incumbent. Source-dependent preparation is performed only by its existing owner.

A host OperationProposal may carry an optional closed `bindings:{fulfillments:[...]}` envelope for `apply` only. It is never part of PlanSubmission or model-visible tool arguments. The dispatcher validates the public effect arguments normally, then attaches this owner metadata as `_fulfillments` to the exact prepared kernel request before final freshness validation and journal persistence. The envelope participates in operation identity and same-call replay. It cannot add an effect or change an effect parameter. Unknown binding kinds or bindings on another verb refuse.

A fulfillment binding selects one exact promise occurrence, its historical source refs and origin scope, actual condition receipts and a complete finite term set. Amounts/quantities come from existing typed values, physical-instance quantities or exact closed numeric source tokens; Jev selects aliases and does not generate numbers. Numeric token syntax proves a position/value only, not its semantic role. Rates, formulas, word-only amounts without a typed scalar, ambiguous units, missing definitions and incomplete reward-term coverage stay unsupported. Existing non-module definitions and instances remain valid rewards through the ordinary define/object authority; module silence never cancels campaign speech.

The kernel validates the promise, origin, terms, effect binding and prior receipt-derived remaining amount before any batch writes. It attaches the fulfillment link to the actual staged cash/item/object receipt, copying that receipt's actual delta/quantity/instance. The link stores bounded terms and source provenance; there is no reward ledger or mutable promise counter. Readers derive open/partial/complete and remaining values from deduplicated canonical effect receipts. Different occurrence IDs remain independent. The same call replays its recorded result; a fresh call cannot overpay or fulfill a completed occurrence again. Every term must reach zero before the whole promise is complete. Recall remains read-only, and disabling typed routing preserves accepted effects and links.

Required implementation owners include the existing apply transaction and memory/capsule projections in addition to the initially proposed helper paths: atomic attachment and a real reader cannot be implemented solely in a new helper. These are required T12 acceptance paths, not a separate state store or scope expansion.

### T14 presentation reference protocol

Character, map and UI presentation use `presentation-reference-v1` for newly generated artifacts. The host issues a pinned `text:n` catalog. A presenter returns one operation per alias: `keep` or `translate` with newly generated text. A keep operation is resolved byte-for-byte by the host; copied source-string keys and unchanged-value reproduction are removed from the model contract. Required aliases are complete/unique, unknown aliases refuse, and current cache/output readers retain their existing materialized map shape. Existing cache seeds remain readable. Translation stays with the existing tool-enabled Pi presenter, in the open campaign language; no language table/detection is introduced and no additional classifier call is required.

Protected syntax already owned by a presenter (such as UI placeholders and rule notation) is represented by host-issued token aliases when it must be placed within translated output. The host restores the exact token and validates the existing multiplicity/shape rules. Selection aliases are not a request to copy original token spellings. This is a source-fidelity migration; generated translations, transliterations and explanatory prose remain generated, and quality/cache/performance claims keep their independent gates.

Document presentation uses the same host-reference principle for title/body portions: new `document-presentation-reference-v1` artifacts select keep or generated translation by issued aliases. The existing source owner materializes kept bytes and returns the unchanged document-view/cache shape. Player-edited documents retain their existing bypass. Paragraph/part selection may bound long work, but empty text, line breaks and all kept portions must remain exact; no whole-document copy is requested merely because the source already uses the play language. The existing tool-enabled presenter remains the only generative owner.

Ordinary-apply policy version 2 distinguishes an unresolved optional candidate from a missing required effect. The dependent whole-batch judgment receives both the confirmed selection and every unresolved candidate. It may proceed only when the selected batch covers the full declared goal and the unresolved candidates are dispensable; any required unknown keeps the entire batch unsettled. This prevents an optional extra disclosure from blocking an otherwise complete authorized briefing. Unknown candidates themselves are never executed and no score substitutes for the kernel's final batch validation.

Setup character guidance uses `setup-guidance-reference-v2` for new author/review attempts. The selected opening scene is already host-owned and is materialized directly; the reviewer/author does not retype it. If a guide must be chosen, it selects an issued opening-NPC alias (or explicit none when the source permits no guide). The host supplies the exact original guide name. Opening/advice/handoff remain generated with their existing language and safety requirements. Raw selector artifacts remain retained; accepted guidance keeps the existing five-string consumer shape. Old reviewed bundles remain readable; new fingerprint/cache acceptance must account for the selector protocol and actual opening/guide source fields without silently rewriting stale reviewed seeds.

NPC journal identity selection uses `journal-reference-v2` for newly requested referenced jobs. The kernel issues a pinned recordable-person alias catalog; model output selects `person:n` rather than reproducing a canonical name. The kernel restores that exact identity/name before the existing journal writer and player-safe named/unnamed projection run. Description, exchange and unnamed label remain newly generated in the play language. Old jobs/artifacts remain readable under their existing protocol; a new referenced request must not silently reinterpret a legacy job's raw artifact. There is one writer, one journal, no extra model call and no new world-state authority.

Ordinary-apply policy version 3 supplies the actual operation timing and effect semantics to both decision stages: apply commits supported effects before guarded narration describes them; a clue records knowledge and does not transfer cash/keys/items; move changes the persistent locus; missing advisory check metadata neither adds nor waives a roll. A retained-input paired diagnostic identified the prior false refusal specifically as requiring the NPC line to be narrated before the clue receipt. Supplying the real owner contract changed that diagnostic to the correct commit-before-narrate order. This diagnostic is not play acceptance and introduces no waiver of source, admission or kernel checks.

The TaskHost total attempt ceiling is separate from the existing host inactivity watchdog. The latter is two minutes since activity and exempts an active tool; it is not a two-minute turn budget. The prior experimental 120-second absolute default cancelled a productive continuity reviewer after an apply had settled and its review artifact had been checked. TaskHost now pins a finite 15-minute total ceiling at input acceptance, configurable by `PI_COC_TASK_DEADLINE_MS` (positive integer milliseconds, at most one hour). An explicit caller `deadlineMs` wins unchanged. Children/retries never renew that absolute deadline; cancellation, action/token/cost ceilings and existing transport/inactivity guards remain in force. This corrects lifetime ownership and is not a latency improvement claim.

The fulfillment semantic domain first distinguishes a requested reward from merely asking about terms or accepting a job. It then reads verified original context, current identities/units and actual condition receipts from the private catalog. Independent due, finite-coverage and amount-shape questions must agree: the mere presence of a numeric token does not turn a rate or formula into a fixed total. Every term selects issued identities/scalars; known deferred terms stay in the complete binding, and prior partial terms reuse their original immutable aliases/digest. Only the read-only prepare owner constructs public effect arguments plus private fulfillment bindings, followed by the normal guarded atomic apply. Model-facing private-plan results exclude the catalogs' opaque snapshot/source bindings.

### T14 setup user-input source selection

`setup-input-reference-v1` freezes actual user text fields from the current Pi setup branch at each input epoch. Duplicate messages/text remain separate occurrences. The model selects a whole field or a range between host-issued extended-grapheme aliases; the host derives UTF-16 coordinates and resolves a shared SourceRef without trimming, normalization, substring lookup or first-match re-anchoring. Grapheme segmentation is syntax only. Omitted catalog coverage is explicit, and unavailable old input cannot be reconstructed on restart.

New target-mode `profile.name` uses a source selection or an explicit generated-name object. Unchanged revisions omit name and retain the prior materialized value/provenance. `pending_action` accepts source selection only, with no generated form. The host sends materialized legacy strings plus a private versioned snapshot/epoch/ref envelope. The setup kernel validates scope, epoch, exact source and materialization atomically before writing; the source-bound route never falls back to copied strings. New active selectors expire with the input epoch, while retained source provenance remains historical evidence.

Existing draft/sheet/receipt/prologue/handoff readers keep their string shapes. Legacy drafts and explicitly legacy RPC behavior remain readable; the direct Electron confirm path supplies neither new name nor pending action and remains unchanged. Generated names are not represented as player wording. Whole-field/range source values remain byte-exact; any canonical name policy that needs a changed value must be represented separately instead of silently changing the source-backed field.

### T15 owner integration closure

A typed ordinary domain may return a structured incumbent handoff for a closed unsupported family and exact public verb (`resolve` or `apply`). This ends typed execution for the attempt and releases only those verbs to the existing Keeper tool owner in the same run; it does not authorize an action or bypass admission, source/Mod gates, delivery guards or the canonical kernel journal. A settled typed mutation, pending/unknown settlement, stale/cancelled lease or genuine player-choice boundary cannot hand off. Ordinary actions cannot bypass typed routing through a globally enabled fallback. Handoff is recorded explicitly and is never inferred from an English diagnostic.
