An ordinary resolve route that remains unknown returns a `replan` step with its unresolved needs, retaining the original intent and planning phase without dispatching a settlement. It is not a composing-ready partial result or permission to switch to the incumbent. This matches ordinary apply's unknown-evidence policy; explicit no-roll, player-choice and supported incumbent outcomes retain their distinct behavior.

Here unknown means an explicit semantic choice in a complete validated decision. A missing, rejected, incomplete or unavailable model answer supplies no such verdict; it retains the existing partial/unavailable return without incrementing semantic replans. Neither outcome authorizes a settlement.

Dependent source preparation remains host-internal. Only a tracked canonical operation's actual `material_pending` response can borrow its task lease to invoke the existing source owner with that exact reading request. A plain read plan cannot request preparation. Accepted detail publication returns a private operation/job/module-bound old/new `task_source_revision` advance. The performing lease and ancestors may advance only that exact source binding, once, after validating current scope, original revision and owner identity. Answer-only cache publication, foreign/old jobs, mismatched modules, failures and cancellations produce no advance. The original pending operation retries under its original call identity and runs current admission/Mod gates again. Source publication is not a world receipt.

An adjacent-source prefetch can enqueue a reading before any worker claims it. Under the existing queue mutex, an exact pending operation may bind that matching queued job only when it has zero attempts and no prior task preparation, worker owner, lease or work directory. This is initial ownership, not adoption of running or historical work. The same atomic write binds its private preparation and promotes it to foreground. A different authority, any claimed/running job or retained attempt refuses; only the originally bound publication can advance. The queue's normal deduplication remains intact.

Source publication stores the completed result and its exact source-advance proof with the same authoritative module pointer write. An immutable generation directory written before that pointer is not yet a published source. Cold request/finish replay may recover the exact job/lease-bound completion when the queue update was interrupted; it cannot infer a proof from a newer current revision. A terminal task checkpoint retains source advances and settled receipt identities even after its execution authority has been cancelled.

In-goal replanning uses the existing maximum of two replans under one original input, lease, deadline and budget. Only a classified recoverable outcome proven non-settled can request it. All plan-dependent options and decision keys are attempt-scoped; immutable successful receipts remain visible across attempts and are never rerun. Unknown settlement is reconciled before any retry, not assigned a new identity. Actual missing consent, stale input and repeated no-progress return their explicit boundary. A revised plan may narrow or reorganize the current goal, never expand player intent or renew the deadline.

Every foreground nested model owner uses one explicit host-only provider-budget port backed by the same task lease. Admission completions and tool-enabled Mod/source/presenter subprocesses reserve a finite input/output/cost/action bound before dispatch, inherit cancellation and the absolute deadline, and settle actual assistant usage. Missing/crashed usage retains its conservative reservation; an overrun is recorded and cancels the root. Reader event parsing aggregates actual assistant usage, not elapsed-time or file-size estimates. Main Keeper requests retain their existing hook owner and are not charged twice. Independent background memory/advisory/warm work has a separately bounded owner and never borrows a closed foreground lease. Cached or deterministic work has no provider charge.

Before dependent work, the host holds a non-waitable writer reservation using the last actual provider payload, the completed assistant message, a 32 KiB public plan-result limit and a finite envelope allowance. Dependent calls cannot queue waiting for that held writer budget. The next Keeper request synchronously transfers it into the exact request reservation; any extra payload cost must still fit the original budget. This is a protected allowance, not a promise to fit arbitrary future context. Omitted public evidence is explicit and the full private task record remains retained. Source/resolve/apply/memory-enabled attempts start with 1,000,000 input tokens and 128 actions (plain bounded reads retain 250,000/32); all retain their original $10, 150,000-output and absolute deadline ceilings. These are declared upfront limits, never renewed after failure. Image-bearing nested requests reserve the model's declared context ceiling when no tighter verified vision bound is available.

Source and budget durability decision (2026-09-21): a pending tracked mutation cannot adopt an already queued/running source job without the exact original `task_preparation` authority. Existing unowned/background work keeps its original budget owner; it may complete independently and make the task stale, but cannot mint a retroactive owned-source advance. Before any nested provider dispatch, its reservation must be durably saved for the performing task and every charged ancestor. Storage failure or cancellation before that barrier denies dispatch. Usage refunds may lag conservatively; the persisted reservation remains the recovery bound. Implicit delivery review uses the same foreground provider-budget port as explicit delivery, never a new standalone budget.

Terminal writer accounting decision (2026-09-21): only plan/read/mutation work that requires a following Keeper response holds future-writer room. An already-generated `narrate` or `ask` does not reserve a second writer. Delivery admission and review still reserve and settle their own actual nested-provider usage against the same task; this is not an audit exemption. A review refusal leaves the task undelivered, and any corrective Keeper request must reserve its exact payload/output under the original remaining budget and deadline, or stop without dispatch. Delivery success and cancellation release unused writer escrow; actual dispatched usage is never refunded as escrow.

The closure follows the same narrow principles as [AWS Step Functions redrive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/redrive-executions.html) (preserve successful steps) and [Temporal activity execution](https://github.com/temporalio/documentation/blob/main/docs/encyclopedia/activities/activity-execution.mdx) (external effects require stable idempotency). Unlike a fresh workflow redrive, this game's same-input replan never resets its retry count or budget. These are implementation precedents; the local canonical receipt and real-table evidence remain the acceptance authority.

The selected #99 Mod alignment completes the already accepted D4 core boundary: keeper-pacing full and brief instruct completion only of the player's still-valid selected goal, return at a new unselected decision or goal completion, and treat structural stalls/repeats as advisory inspection. Narration-craft removes its mandatory new-event/multiple-options copy of the old floor. NPC voice already permits direct answers and natural closure; unchanged compliant bytes need no artificial version bump. Any changed package increments its version with state/settings/capabilities unchanged; retained locks and prior package bytes are never rewritten. Existing assembly/on-off/legacy guards prove wiring only. The separately specified real paired pacing A/B remains required before a pacing-improvement claim.

## 123. NPC personality and relationship continuity (#102)

Canonical specification: [NPC personality and relationship spec](specs/npc-personality-and-relationship-spec.md). The player remains the focus. Personality and attributed shared history inform the Keeper's choices; typed advice grants no world effect. This section defines the implemented interfaces. Scoped real-play evidence, regression results and remaining product-acceptance limits are recorded in [the NPC acceptance report](research/npc-implementation-acceptance-20260922.md).

### 123.1 Stable personality owner (#103)

`npc.job {campaign, name?}` is a host-only preparation method. With no name it offers a currently present person lacking an accepted personality; a named request must resolve an existing NPC. It returns `job_id:null` when no preparation is needed, otherwise a durable, scope/source-bound job and a model-safe packet. The host owns job identity, actor identity, source fingerprint and campaign/worldline/loop binding. The author sees a semantic person name, available authored descriptive material and instructions, not host identifiers. Source-authored personality takes precedence; generated personality is an explicitly marked interpretation/supplement, never a new stat, secret, relationship or world event.

`npc.submit {campaign,job_id,claim,personality:{description}}` accepts a bounded nonempty description for the exact current job. It publishes an immutable accepted entry in core `world.npc_character`, keyed by the canonical NPC identity, with its origin, exact source fingerprint, scope, author-job identity and submitted-content digest. Accepted personality is not owned by an optional Mod. Existing `table.look focus:npc` and `present` project it as `personality:{description,origin}`; the private storage envelope does not enter model context.

The existing campaign RPC writer lock covers claim/publication only, never author model execution. Publication stores the acceptance result and content digest in the same authoritative world write. The job completion file is a recoverable secondary view: identical submit after an interrupted completion repairs it and returns the same accepted result; changed submit refuses. A changed source or worldline/loop refuses a stale result. A completed personality is not rerolled by restart or later preparation, and a later source disagreement stays visible rather than silently overwriting accepted material.

`npc.fail {campaign,job_id,claim,reason}` marks that job's failed attempt without accepting its draft. The background owner may explicitly reclaim failed work with the same job identity and original source binding; current in-flight work is not replaced by an unrelated claim. An unfinished job remains recoverable after shutdown. Ordinary play reads existing material while preparation is pending and never waits for a full NPC profile.

Producer: a tool-enabled Pi author working on an owned preparation packet. Writer: the core NPC publication owner. Readers: NPC look, capsule and later NPC decision tasks. Actor: the ordinary Keeper, still subject to canonical effect and delivery guards. Source/shape/lifecycle tests do not prove semantic personality quality or genuine player experience.

A job packet also returns a host-only `claim` token. Reclaiming a failed logical job retains its job identity but mints a new claim; submit and fail must carry the current claim. A late prior attempt cannot publish or retire the replacement attempt. The author never receives either host token.

### 123.2 Directed relationship evidence and limited perspective (#104)

The existing memory owner remains the writer of attributed relationship, belief, knowledge and promise records. NPC projection now reads directed relationship rows whose subject resolves to this NPC and whose single target remains explicit. It retains source authority, attribution, epistemic state, valid turn and fulfillment evidence; it neither reduces them to party stance nor promotes a report to world truth.

`present[].relationships` and `table.look focus:npc` expose bounded current evidence grouped by target. `recent_speech` contains this NPC's exact committed speech, with its turn and attribution, even when memory extraction has not completed. Those words are conversation reports, not automatic relationship changes or knowledge grants. No semantic parsing of dialogue, implied audience or names is performed in code.

Host-only `npc.perspectives {campaign,name?}` reads the requested person or the current onstage set from one campaign snapshot, avoiding repeated whole-campaign reads before parallel decisions. Its `views` are still separate NPC perspectives, never a shared model context. `npc.perspective {campaign,name}` remains the single-person read and freshness check. It returns this person's personality, own authored goals/fears, authored knowledge and beliefs, explicit memory reports whose knowers include this person, directed relationship evidence and their own recent speech. Other people's private memories, party-only discoveries, Keeper notes and the full room's private capsule are absent. A missing relationship is unknown rather than a fabricated neutral score. The response binds a host-issued view revision to the source, scope and supplied current evidence; later decision tasks must recheck it before adoption.

The generative memory instruction and typed memory-write policy version 4 explicitly preserve relationship direction and the supporting event, while refusing to infer durable trust from courtesy alone. The NPC perspective also includes promises this person made or explicitly knows about, with canonical fulfillment projection; knowing of a promise does not fulfill it.

The capsule does not repeat an identical promise occurrence in both history.promises and commitments. Deduplication uses host-owned memory identity; the named NPC read and decision perspective retain full attribution and commitments. New optional detail must not displace the same existing evidence through duplication.

Raw committed speech is the immediate fallback while the existing extraction job is pending. It does not stall foreground play, claim that an unrecorded favor happened or substitute the player's assertions for settled effects. Onstage response generation and Jev see this limited projection; the Keeper still has its ordinary separate private context and retains effect authority.

### 123.3 Prepared responses and concurrent choice (#105)

Host-only npc.responses.job/submit use the same campaign publication owner and per-attempt claim law as personality preparation. A tool-enabled author receives only the limited NPC perspective and supplies a bounded list of conditional intentions, never finished dialogue or world effects. Accepted response banks are derived job artifacts scoped to the NPC, source/personality, scene and worldline; they do not mutate canonical world state. Publication is idempotent and a replaced claim cannot overwrite a newer bank. Missing or stale banks leave ordinary Keeper play available.

The existing look verb gains optional evaluate_responses:true for focus:npc. A name requests that NPC; omission explicitly requests the present NPCs. The normal NPC view remains the result; a private NPC host bridge appends advisory typed results. No new public verb or mandatory planning round is introduced. The Keeper may answer directly from current material and can use this read when weighing alternatives. Missing banks are prepared in the background; this read never waits for their author.

All requested, ready NPC batches use one shared-auth decision adapter owned by the NPC session, with configurable shared Jev concurrency. Each compatible view batches candidate fit, situational applicability and closed Choice questions; independent NPC batches dispatch concurrently. Same-batch Choice does not consume same-batch scores. The current canonical player input is data, not an already settled action. Model state excludes private host bindings and other NPC perspectives. A selected response is returned only after its view revision is revalidated; unavailable, stale, partial and none-of-the-above remain explicit. Root provider budgets, when present, reserve and settle the nested Jev calls, while optional authoring uses its own background budget.

The choice result never executes an effect or authorizes player action. It cannot require confirmation of an already chosen player goal, force continued conversation or create debt for unused advice. Source generation, secret disclosure, mechanics and delivery keep their existing owners.

A configured NPC session may supply the same advice automatically once per actual player-input epoch. This is a bounded context supplement, not an approval gate: preparation is never awaited, ready peers can be included independently, and the foreground grace period defaults to 1250 ms (PI_COC_NPC_ADVICE_WAIT_MS, maximum 2000; zero or PI_COC_NPC_ADVICE_AUTO=0 disables it). Expiry cancels remaining decision work and ordinary Keeper play continues. The bounded private message is composed before the existing context-budget owner, reports omissions and expires after a tool result or new input; it is not carried as future narrative debt. Explicit look evaluation remains available. This wait and its actual adoption must be measured in #107 rather than called a speedup.

### 123.4 On-demand reunion continuity (#106)

An NPC view offers reunion only when this person is currently present, a prior committed meaningful encounter exists, an intervening committed absence exists and positive game time elapsed. The kernel derives the interval from actual committed presence/speech/receipts and the game clock; the model never invents interval identifiers or intermediate turns. The offer carries the last known encounter and elapsed time, with existing personality, directed evidence and commitments beside it.

The tool-enabled Keeper can generate a modest continuation during its ordinary work and establish it with the existing apply npc effect: reunion contains bounded background, reports and open_threads arrays of new English Keeper-facing strings. Background is table-established continuity, reports remain this NPC's attributed claims, and open_threads are possibilities, not player obligations. An unchanged quiet interval is valid. The effect cannot create a person, change game parameters, move or transfer anything, fulfill a promise, or combine with another NPC mutation; actual effects require their existing operations. Source facts and player decisions remain authoritative.

The existing apply transaction writes one core character reunion record and a canonical NPC receipt. Same-interval identical content reuses the accepted record; different content refuses instead of rewriting the past. Derived summaries and memory continue after delivery. Reading later encounters reuses accepted continuity and never reruns offstage simulation. A new return after another genuine absence has its own interval. This path adds no foreground author subprocess: the current Keeper already is a tool-enabled Pi agent and only the minimal canonical acceptance is synchronous.

Reunion extend true appends only new compatible detail while retaining every already accepted line; the host performs the merge, so the Keeper never copies old prose to preserve it. Ordinary establishment with different content for the same interval still refuses. Each receipt states reuse or extension without fabricating intermediate events.

The automatic input supplement asks only the closed Choice and candidate-premise judgments required to offer a response. Diagnostic personality/relationship Scores remain batched in an explicit evaluate_responses read or diagnostic run; a score nobody consumes is not made a foreground dependency. A no-fit result requests one background candidate refresh per NPC/input, using the person's updated limited perspective after delivery, without making the Keeper wait. A repeated host continuation does not start another automatic evaluation for the same canonical input.

## 124. Jev preselection supplies actual material before the Keeper request (#108)

Status: contract frozen for implementation; functional, semantic, performance and packaged-product acceptance remain separate pending gates. This section extends the optional preselection in §5 under the authority and exact SourceRef rules of §122. The implementation specification is [Jev prescreen material supply](specs/jev-prescreen-material-supply.md).

### 124.1 Existing workspace read, versioned material view

`table.workspace.read` retains its ordinary response and the legacy `preselect:true` response. Host-only `preselect:{version:2,mode:"catalog"|"read"|"check"|"index",keys?:string[],cursor?:number,limit?:number,priority?:string[]}` opts into actual material supply (`index` and `priority` are defined in §124.10). `query`, `names` and the expected `binding` remain outer request fields. Keys and cursors are host navigation data, not model-authored references or a new authority. Unsupported modes/fields, foreign scope and stale expected bindings refuse or return an explicit unavailable/stale view. No request enters a game mutation or legacy repair path.

The versioned response retains `status`, `authority` and `binding`, and adds `materials:{version:2,candidates,coverage,next?}`. A candidate carries `key`, `kind`, `label`, `summary`, `authority`, `coverage`, actual `body` or `data` when materialized, and an ordinary semantic `read` follow-up when available. A host-only executable descriptor uses the existing `method`/`params` fields. Shared exact `SourceRef` values may travel in private `refs`; a catalog key or locator alone is never source proof. Model projection supplies semantic aliases, actual content and useful provenance, not raw paths, hashes, private identities or offsets.

`catalog` returns bounded candidates and actual usable content or an explicit materialization descriptor; `read` materializes only keys issued by the current matching catalog/binding; `check` verifies relevant revisions without constructing the full material catalog or capsule. Every bound claim is based on actual owner state. The view reports inspected, emitted, omitted and unavailable scope per family, including all intermediate truncation; a limit never implies completeness.

The workspace owner supplies graph entities with the required authored properties/relations, real rule clauses and dependency groups, committed records, and real current read descriptors. A rule-family index is navigation rather than a clause. Table records are not dropped because their existing content field is named `text`. Graph projection completeness never implies entity or question completeness. Existing ordinary workspace projections remain compatible.

Catalog discovery may query the existing rule/catalog owner directly using the current query, without requiring an inventory instance. Memory and original attributed history use the existing `memory.evidence` snapshot/page/original/finish operations where necessary; the preselector does not implement another memory truth store or classify meaning through keyword lists. Selected evidence is checked by its original owner. Current PC/NPC/object/session details use the existing read-only projections; the core capsule is not screened out.

The material binding additionally covers `memory_revision`, `npc_revision`, `records_revision` and `catalog_revision` where those sources participate. Memory evidence uses its existing source/index/world revision checks. NPC revision includes the ledger and journal material actually read; records bind committed content; catalog revision binds actual accepted catalog data, not an assumed unrelated manifest. An unknown dependency is unavailable, not silently current. The existing snapshot cache may reuse unchanged file bytes/identities; computing a check must not run a model or reread the whole PDF.

### 124.2 Source material through the existing source owner

`module.source.materials.snapshot {campaign,module_id,answer_limit?,answer_cursor?}` is a host-only read served by the existing campaign-aware module owner. It extends the current source snapshot with `answers_revision`, `checked_answers`, `checked_answers_omitted`, `checked_answers_invalid` and an optional continuation. Original `pdf`, file identity, page count, generation and revision remain private to the host. The same existing campaign-local versus library routing applies; the preselector never chooses a module directory itself.

Checked answer entries include the saved `question`, `focus`, actual supported answer/limitations, original page references and the existing integrity-checked evidence envelope. New accepted answers retain question/focus in their existing acceptance record. Historical entries may recover those fields from a uniquely matching original completed answer task; ambiguous or absent association remains unattributed and is explicitly omitted from semantic enumeration. Source SHA, context generation and draft/review bytes are verified exactly as for the existing answer peek. Enumeration creates no publication or world mutation.

When the existing source owner first seeds a campaign-private module from the same accepted library generation, compatible checked answers may accompany that immutable seed. The owner copies only integrity-verified draft/review artifacts and their accepted source/generation/question/focus metadata into the private module. Historical task attribution must be uniquely recovered before copying; invalid or ambiguous entries are omitted explicitly. Artifact containment and original/copy digests are checked under the existing seed/metadata publication locks, and the private directory remains atomically published. Source jobs, queues, leases, task publication receipts and mutable hard links are never inherited. A later private generation must still pass ordinary answer compatibility checks; this does not allow consultation across mismatched campaign sources or merge later library state into an already private module.

The host source provider uses the runtime already delivered on `coc:kernel-bridge`: `home`, `sourceInfo`, `sourceSearch` and `sourceText`. Its input is the current campaign/module binding, question, cancellation and bounded candidate/material allowance. Its output is actual source candidates, explicit searched/omitted/empty/error coverage, a source read set and a revalidation operation. It must work without the broader TaskRuntime/PlanPacket product toggle. It reuses native source catalogs, SourceRef resolution and the existing native-consultation eligibility decisions; it does not create another source owner, queue or generative reader.

Discovery represents the original document beyond graph entities. Small documents may use wide native-page access. Long documents combine existing source navigation/current citations, bounded literal search and budgeted broader page access; literal search is only one channel and cannot be the sole cross-language/paraphrase discovery path. Pages not inspected or content omitted from candidate previews remain explicit and addressable. Batches and further access share one deadline and budget. A missed/empty native match never proves source absence.

Raw native candidates remain `native_text` with partial, unsupported consultation coverage. To replace a generative factual consultation, preselection must reuse the existing source owner's native-consultation policy and proof issuer. The policy is shared with `native-source-domain`: plaintext eligibility, evidence classification of exact parts, and sufficient coverage of the same question and selected parts under its existing size bound. A general prescreen `necessary/helpful` choice or mixed-material coverage assessment is not this approval. Shared pure policy builders and selection validation may be extracted from that owner; no fabricated TaskView or parallel policy is permitted. Independent eligibility and relevance decisions may share a batch; dependent coverage consumes their actual results.

Only the shared source-owned materializer can return `native_consultation` authority for a validated selection. It rechecks the source binding, file identity/page count, exact active references and native extraction version before returning the existing proof and exact excerpts. Canonical `source.excerpts` and prescreen use this same materializer. The Keeper projection records the precise qualified question, actual excerpts, used/omitted/unknown coverage, `supported: true` for that bounded consultation, and `prepared: false`; private refs remain host-only. It grants no image/layout proof, graph/entity/readiness publication, player knowledge or execution authority. Qualification calls spend the same remaining prescreen decision/token/cost/deadline budget, independent of the broader TaskRuntime product toggle. Visual, preparation, uncertain, missing-context, timeout or failed-validation outcomes retain honest raw partial material or the existing follow-up path; they never silently promote it. A changed question cannot inherit the old qualification.

Selected native content is resolved from exact current page snapshots. Search snippets remain navigation-only. The existing source mode distinction (`plaintext`, `visual`, `preparation`, `uncertain`) and source support/coverage constraints apply before native-extractive consultation is represented as supported. A useful partial raw excerpt may be supplied with its exact origin and explicit unverified/partial status, but cannot mint a supported answer, visual observation or playable readiness. Native text cannot settle map geometry, layout-dependent facts or new executable parameters. Visual and preparation gaps carry the ordinary source lookup continuation; only the incumbent reader/reviewer and preparation owner can satisfy them.

### 124.3 Actual context, selection and bounded supplementation

`preparePrescreen` consumes `suppliedMessages` from the actual projected baseline, `byteBudget`, current campaign/binding/capsule, and the optional narrow source runtime/module identity, in addition to its existing call/signal/telemetry/decision inputs. It returns the existing optional custom message. Preparation metadata stays in `details.prescreen`; no preparation event asserts delivery.

Candidate selection sees actual content or explicitly partial previews and the relevant current retained history/tool results, not only generic names. Unknown or unrepresented context is never declared already supplied. Host exact range/content deduplication may skip unchanged already-retained material without a Jev call; a different query or dependency invalidates applicable decision reuse. Repeated requests for the same input, baseline and read set share in-flight/prepared work.

A successful dynamic owner read replaces the catalog's `material_not_read` placeholder with materialized-read coverage. Preserve any real owner omissions and keep bounded projection completeness unknown when the owner does not claim completeness. Do not mark a whole NPC, character, object or session complete merely because its read succeeded, and do not send an unread marker beside its actual returned body. Failed reads and memory finish coverage retain their own outcomes.

Jev performs bounded choices over issued candidates using the shared adapter and lease. Independent same-state groups may run concurrently; dependent judgments use the actual results of the preceding read. After materialization, unresolved useful gaps may trigger limited further selection when the remaining budget allows it. No progress, cancellation or budget exhaustion ends optional work with explicit remaining gaps. No mandatory second round, perfect selection, fixed optimal set or new player decision is implied.

The optional allowance starts once, at the first eligible prescreen opportunity after mandatory baseline preparation for the accepted input. It is one absolute deadline, never renewed by tool results, repeated context hooks, retries or invalidation within that input. Mandatory gameplay preparation is measured separately rather than silently exhausting this allowance before optional work starts. The allowance is the configured per-input preparation budget of §124.10 (twelve seconds by default; originally six), additional optional waiting that is measured, not a player-facing SLA. Semantic calls use a narrower child deadline, leaving room inside the original outer deadline for materialization and final owner validation. Completed independent decisions may produce an incomplete packet when another group or optional coverage/supplement step times out; unfinished work becomes explicit unknown gaps, not a negative relevance verdict. Parent cancellation, a stale owner, or an expired outer deadline still prevents publication. No partial packet bypasses any final source, memory or workspace check. Stage timing and candidate counts distinguish discovery, decisions, reads and final validation so a bounded timeout cannot masquerade as useful delivery.

The G1–G8 distinctions in the specification govern this family: purpose, conjunction, actual possession of context, redundancy/complementarity, correction/currentness, attribution/evidence direction, public/spatial scope, and unknown versus relevant conflict. A `skip` on uncertain evidence cannot be represented as a proven absence. Rule indexes, partial excerpts and failed reads do not satisfy a complete-material claim.

### 124.4 Final request and telemetry

The final projection accounts for actual system/tools/output reserve and protects current input, capsule and tool pairing. Workspace is first tested against the real budget; only bodies retained in that baseline count as supplied. If any later projection removes a relied-upon body, the host cancels that availability claim and repacks an appropriate piece or reports a missing follow-up. A prepared-but-dropped workspace must not suppress the only copy of required evidence.

The host checks source/state/dependency versions before using a cached packet and before returning the final request. Background memory/NPC journal changes participate even when world/turn identity is unchanged. Session reset/resume/fork/switch and cancellation discard inappropriate work; stale results never enter another request. Failure of optional preselection leaves the original gameplay and guarded read paths usable.

Final telemetry is generated from the actual outgoing message set: request correlation, prepared packet correlation, retained material identities/digests/coverage, omitted material/reasons, candidate scope and costs. `prepared`, `read` and `delivered` are different events. Subsequent reads distinguish already-delivered content from genuinely new evidence. Actual semantic use is established by source/request/tool/final-delivery review, not inferred from an injection counter. These observations never become future obligations or action authority.

The existing public Pi `before_provider_request` hook confirms packet presence after context projection and provider message conversion. It observes without rewriting the payload and records only bounded correlation/content digests and retention status, never arbitrary headers, credentials or the full private payload. A packet not confirmed in that payload is not counted as delivered merely because the context hook returned it. No private Pi patch or replacement stream loop is introduced.

### 124.5 Activation, compatibility and acceptance

The existing Jev extension adds an optional boolean `ext.jev.preselectEnabled` setting, default false. Feature state and credential availability are read separately through the existing extension configuration owner. An explicit source-CLI `PI_COC_JEV_PRESELECT=0|1` remains a development override only; managed sessions obey their mounted extension settings and credentials. A saved key alone does not enable the feature, and an unmounted extension cannot be revived by inherited values. Status reports configured/enabled/active without exposing secrets.

Consultation reuse must eliminate redundant source-answer work when valid evidence supports the question, while actual required entity/parameter/graph preparation retains its existing ownership and publication guards. Existing accepted preparation, completed publication and pending same-purpose work are consulted through those owners, never replayed by the preselector. This section does not authorize new writes, altered source-generation rules or longer hidden waits.

Acceptance follows the actual outgoing Keeper request and canonical real-player table seams. Every material family and G1–G8 target is traced independently; matched Haunting, short-PDF and long-PDF results include quality, repeated/new reads and complete player wait. Build changes or unequal source/preparation/cache states cannot support direct same-state causal claims. Functional source acceptance, performance acceptance and the canonical installed App are separately reported.

### 124.6 Adaptive read-only prescreen loop

The optional prescreener may continue through a request-local `discover` / `read` / `follow` / `finish` loop. Its fixed tool vocabulary operates on a dynamic frontier of owner-issued candidates. The host owns executable arguments, private keys, pagination and source bindings; Jev chooses semantic operation aliases using the existing DecisionAdapter and TaskLease. No new public gameplay tool, RPC authority, generated search plan or world mutation is introduced.

Every dependent decision sees actual preceding observations and the retained materials. `discover` advances a bound catalog or source page; `read` materializes selected candidates through their existing owners; `follow` expands a structured source relationship or source-owned reference from already read material. Exact existing names may be copied by the host. Prose is never parsed with semantic keyword lists to manufacture links. Newly discovered material is eligible in subsequent decisions even when absent from the initial candidate pool. A fixed initial candidate list with repeated rankings does not satisfy this contract.

The existing v2 catalog accepts an optional `entity` semantic handle in `preselect`, only with mode `catalog`. It enumerates that exact entity's source units within the same bound graph, retaining the same keys, references and readiness as the ordinary catalog. It neither expands scope nor resolves invented names. Empty or truncated results carry explicit coverage. The host obtains the handle from an issued material's module read descriptor or structured relation; Jev does not author it. This focused navigation avoids scanning unrelated catalog pages to follow one known reference.

The existing source provider also exposes a host-only `readNativePages` continuation over at most two valid unmaterialized pages per operation. It reuses the exact native snapshot/SourceRef materializer and the captured PDF/extraction binding. The loop offers adjacent pages of retained excerpts and a bounded next-page continuation. These new excerpts remain raw partial native evidence; they do not inherit a different excerpt's consultation qualification or visual verification. A changed extraction or source rejects publication, and all calls remain inside the original prescreen allowance.

The existing `coc-prescreen` payload remains the output schema: `materials` contain actual owner-projected content, attribution, authority, provenance and coverage; `gaps` retain unsupported or unread parts and ordinary read continuations. Source relationships remain in their attributed materials. An additive `retrieval:{version:1,status:"ready"|"partial",stop_reason,steps}` describes the optional retrieval attempt, never game readiness or source publication. `assessment` describes only the final retained evidence. Model decisions select content; the host builds and validates the packet. Operation identities and traces remain private in `details.prescreen` and bounded telemetry.

Host material dependency keys remain private in catalog/read metadata. Jev and Keeper coverage projections express an entity context requirement using its existing semantic name, never the internal graph-unit key. Truncated operation frontiers and gap previews report their omitted counts to the decision model. Optional retrieval diagnostics may remain in private packet metadata when including them would evict actual evidence from the final request.

Already-supported cases retain the direct path. A loop shares the original absolute optional deadline, provider allowance, read count and finalization reserve. It never renews an allowance. Unchanged work is not executed twice; a cycle producing neither new material nor a new candidate frontier stops. Finish, no progress, exhausted frontier, budget, provider failure and packing limits return useful current partial material with explicit gaps. Parent cancellation, stale bindings or outer-deadline expiry still prohibit publication. Additional reads invalidate earlier sufficiency judgments. Packet reuse after context/dependency changes removes the old retrieval assessment together with the old coverage assessment.

Acceptance must show a dependent owner-backed discovery chain entering the actual converted Keeper request, plus cancellation, stale-state rejection, finite budget and no-progress termination. Deterministic loop tests do not establish Jev semantic quality, Keeper adoption or latency improvement; those remain separate real-provider and canonical-play gates.

Optimization decision (2026-09-22): coverage and next-operation selection share one frozen-state decision; there is no preceding coverage-only round when operations remain. Within that same request, independent inclusion questions may nominate additional already-issued reads. The host runs at most four reads with distinct host-owned concurrency keys together; discovery, follow operations, shared memory-session work and any operation needing new parameters remain sequential. Inclusion answers do not consume another answer from their batch. Reads produce staged results; the host applies successful stages in issued order so network completion order cannot decide which evidence survives the byte budget. All sibling work settles or is cancelled before another observation/decision or final validation. Invalidated or stale results still prevent publication. Catalog candidates with an already materialized complete body and no deferred owner read are reused directly; final owner validation is mandatory. Telemetry distinguishes decision rounds, operation count, simultaneous width and elapsed wall time rather than summing overlapping reads as latency.

### 124.7 Material supply regression closeout

Request budgeting uses Pi's public `convertToLlm` message projection plus the existing system/tool/output reserves. Host-only `details`, correlation keys and cached provenance remain available to host consumers but do not consume the model-message allowance. Internal artifact/storage byte limits still use the raw object size. Baseline selection, supplement allowance, final projection and request telemetry use the same message-size operation; no component substitutes the stored envelope for the sent content.

Graph catalog ordering preserves a bounded coherent front for each prioritized entity: its identity, first authored unit and first relationship unit precede the next entity's corresponding front. Further units remain addressable through deterministic pagination and focused entity navigation. This avoids a page of identity-only cards without allowing one large entity to consume the whole first page. Unit completeness remains distinct from entity or question completeness. Relationship delivery is verified across actual supplied units for the same entity, not by expecting all fields in the first identity card.

When a material packet is tight, gap descriptions may use a compact form retaining the semantic reason and usable continuation. Required explanation for retained partial/unqualified material is not replaced solely by a diagnostic count. Redundant coverage/provenance may stay in host metadata; genuinely omitted optional gaps remain counted. Final packet size and actual provider retention are checked after this projection. Tests must use valid typed provider answers and verify the delivered material/limitations rather than an obsolete envelope layout.

### 124.8 Jev agent owns optional preload and a fixed Keeper support contract

The user replaces the two-stage preload selector with the shared read-only Jev evidence agent. When Jev preload is active, the old optional workspace selection/reranking path does not run alongside it. Current authoritative capsule, source/package instructions and retained history remain mandatory host context. The agent owns selection from the first issued operation, including discovery, independent reads, source consultation and follow-up; there is no unconditional legacy candidate-classification pass before its loop. The semantic locate stage of §124.10 is the agent's own first discovery over the complete closed entity index, not that legacy pass: it only orders discovery and names what the host reads, and it never counts as reading or coverage.

The shared runtime accepts a versioned semantic request `{schema_version:1,purpose:"preload"|"lookup"|"classify",query:string}`. Scope, current context, owner ports, source references, deadlines and budgets are host-bound execution options, never model-authored identity or authority. Preload binds query to the exact accepted player input. Keeper-initiated lookup consumes this interface through section 124.9; classify remains available to future consumers. This does not activate the macro-plan protocol or replace the narrower direct/semantic recall contracts.

Every supplied Keeper packet has one validated envelope: `schema_version`, `kind:"keeper_support"`, `turn`, `request`, `authority:"advisory"`, `complete:false`, `parameters`, `materials`, `assessment`, `gaps`, `retrieval`, `check`, `coverage` and `note`. Parameters always contains `scene`, `people`, `objects`, `rules`, `history` and `source` arrays of host-issued material aliases; an empty slot means not supplied, never that the world lacks that subject. Materials carry actual owner-projected content and provenance. Slot membership comes from existing closed owner kinds, not language or name heuristics. The host validates unique aliases and every slot reference after final packing. Assessment always contains coverage and consistency, with explicit uncertain defaults; retrieval may be null when no successful decision was obtained. Missing facts or mechanics are not fabricated to fill required fields.

The host builds this envelope from actual reads and typed Jev judgments. The Keeper receives concise schema guidance and consumes the fixed slots plus material contents, while retaining its ordinary read, narration, admission and settlement interfaces. Candidate keys, exact SourceRefs and coordination traces stay in private metadata. Budgeting includes the complete fixed envelope from the first packing trial. Verbose diagnostics and repeated check basis yield to actual evidence; an oversized check suggestion becomes unknown. Final packing revalidates all remaining aliases and never exceeds its message allowance. Public gaps have a bounded first/tail window and counted omissions, with the complete gap set retained privately. Large operation frontiers retain an explicit index-navigation operation when question packing omits tools. Memo reuse validates the same schema and removes stale assessments; legacy packets cannot masquerade as the new contract.

Acceptance must establish that the first retrieval model request is the agent operation decision, the legacy optional preload does not duplicate it, and the actual converted Keeper request contains a schema-valid packet with correct references. Preserve existing cancellation, stale-source, parallel-read, native/visual distinction, memory-original/finish, compact-gap and private-metadata guards. Retrieval classifications remain advisory; adding mechanical recommendations requires its own accepted owner and validation seam.

The user explicitly includes ordinary-check recommendations in this packet. A required `check` field contains the existing `check_preflight` advice shape, including advisory disposition, optional issued action template and unresolved needs; it always declares `authorization:"advisory_only"` and `settled:false`. The existing ordinary route/profile policy and resolve-options owner produce the suggestion under the same preparation budget. Public prior dialogue may supply context; private retrieved evidence cannot supply consent. Campaign, worldline, loop, turn, exact input and options revisions are checked before delivery. Every read/decision/final check is bounded by the caller's signal and deadline. Independent final owner checks overlap after all retrieval and check-preparation decisions end; optional check advice has a slightly earlier final deadline so it cannot hold verified material past publication. Missing, stale or unsupported advice becomes explicit unknown without discarding independently valid materials. No preflight path invokes resolve/apply or supplies rolled outcomes. Final action authorization and numeric results remain with admission and the canonical kernel.

### 124.9 Keeper-initiated support lookup

`lookup {kind:"support",query:string}` is the Keeper-facing entry to the same evidence agent used for preload. It accepts a nonempty question of at most 2048 characters; other lookup-specific options are rejected rather than silently ignored. The normal seven verbs remain unchanged. Exact module/rule/catalog lookup, source preparation and direct/semantic recall keep their existing owners and result contracts. A support lookup can retrieve across their read-only material catalogs, including retained memory originals, without recursively calling the public support tool or enabling macro-plan mode.

The host binds the current campaign/capsule/worldline/loop/turn, builds a `SupportRequest` with purpose lookup, and runs the shared preparation implementation. The query describes evidence the Keeper needs; it never replaces the accepted player's action for check advice. No active player action means unknown check advice, even if the Keeper's query asks for a roll. Result content is the schema-validated keeper_support v1 object. Host references, checkpoints and traces remain private. Valid partial results preserve gaps, including explicit provider unavailability. A cancelled, stale or unpublishable preparation returns a normal tool refusal and cannot publish an old packet or mutate the world.

Explicit support lookup requires the existing configured and mounted Jev integration, independently of the automatic-preload switch. Each requested call has the configured preparation allowance and decision budget of §124.10 (twelve seconds and twenty-four decisions by default), further restricted and charged by any existing foreground task provider budget. Cancellation and final owner validation are the same as preload. The canonical dispatcher requires lookup.support for tracked callers; the tool does not acquire capabilities absent from its parent. Preparation performs only existing read methods, never resolve/apply, source authoring or publication. The ordinary tool result reaches the Keeper's next request and is then available to existing exact-content deduplication.

Acceptance follows an actual Pi tool call through the canonical dispatcher and the next converted provider request, including fresh query binding, a valid packet, private metadata exclusion, stale/cancelled refusal, and unchanged direct lookup/recall behavior. A module-level call alone is insufficient to prove this consumer.

### 124.10 Semantic locate over the closed entity index, honest packing and a per-input budget (2026-09-22)

A real Chinese-language Haunting table showed two different player questions receiving byte-identical first catalog pages: graph discovery ranked candidates by character-pair postings of the raw player sentence against English authored prose, which never matched, so ordering fell back to scene, present people and insertion order. The user's ruling: a semantic model must not be fed through a tokenizer. This section replaces the lexical query channel as the way preload and support lookup reach module material. It adds no word list, language detection, translation table or other tokenizer; localization is Jev's own typed judgment over a host-issued closed set.

**Index.** `preselect:{version:2,mode:"index"}` returns, under the same binding checks as `catalog`, `materials:{version:2,candidates:[],coverage:{},index:{entities,rules,entities_total,rules_total,omitted}}`. Each entity is `{handle,label,kind,summary}` for one node of the effective published graph: `handle` is its existing semantic name (the one `lookup module` and `preselect.entity` accept), `label` its display name, `summary` its authored summary clipped to 320 characters; a summary that only restates the name is replaced by the first authored prose, description, dramatic question, agenda or Keeper note (normalized name comparison, never a semantic judgment). Each rule is `{name,label,family}` for one clause of the current rule graph. The index is independent of the query, bounded (2048 entities, 512 rules) and reports omissions; it never reads a PDF, runs a model or mutates state.

**Locate.** The host partitions the index mechanically into batches (at most 64 cards and 14 KB of cards per batch) and asks, per card, one Noul: is this entity's authored material (or this rule clause) likely needed or materially useful for at least one part of the request, given the request and a bounded current context (location, present people, the last verified public quotes). Batches are independent same-state questions and run concurrently through the shared adapter under the one preparation lease; this follows the vendor fan-out, semantic-find, passage-classification and rerank patterns (one bounded state, many independent typed questions, parallel requests). Jev sees aliases (`entity_N`, `rule_N`) with name, kind and summary; the host maps aliases back to its own handles. A batch that times out, fails or returns a malformed answer leaves its cards unjudged; unjudged is never irrelevant.

**Use of the locate result.** Cards with noul at least 0.35 are ranked (the vendor semantic-find starting boundary between absent and partially addressed); at most 24 entity handles travel as `preselect.priority` and at most 8 rule names join `rules`. `priority` is ordering for `catalog` (and `read`, so the same issued keys stay addressable): the named handles lead graph discovery in the given order, before the current scene, established names and present people; unknown handles are ignored and counted; it never filters, widens scope or resolves invented names. In material mode the query string no longer orders graph discovery; without a priority the order is structural and the coverage says so (`graph_entity.ranking:"structural"|"semantic_locate"`). Named rules become rule materials ahead of the rule owner's own query lookup, which remains that owner's ordinary behavior. Entities judged at least 0.7 (the vendor found boundary), at most four, have their complete catalog units materialized by the host before the first loop decision, through the same staged publication, byte trial and final owner validation as any read; the agent then judges coverage on actual content and may follow or finish. Weaker located entities are only ordered first in the frontier. The loop no longer spends decisions opening fixed four-candidate index groups; read operations are offered in discovery (located) order on the existing 48-operation frontier page with its navigation operation, the first sixteen with a 320-character content preview and the rest with label and kind.

**Packing.** Jev 1.13 accepts 64k tokens per request and 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question (typesafe models page); the tokenizer is not published. `packDecisionBatch` keeps UTF-8 JSON bytes as a provable token upper bound (provenance unchanged, `utf8_json_bytes_token_upper_bound`) and checks it against those two documented limits, taking "k" as 1000 to stay conservative (`requestLimit: 64000`, `stateQuestionLimit: 32000`). The estimate is not a token count; telemetry records the summed upper bound next to provider-reported input tokens so the ratio is observable. Nothing unchanged is duplicated inside one request: the supplied-context preview excludes the capsule already carried by the capsule overview, operation previews omit the entity stub repeated in every graph unit, and locate batches carry no materials or operations while loop batches carry no index. Jev requests are stateless, so the request, bounded current context and retained materials are still sent with every decision that judges them.

**Budget.** The preload allowance is one per-input budget read through the existing Jev extension configuration owner: `ext.jev.preselectAllowanceMs` (source-CLI development override `PI_COC_JEV_PRESELECT_ALLOWANCE_MS`), default 12000 ms, clamped to 2000–30000 ms, with a matching per-input decision budget of 24 Jev requests. It starts once at the first eligible context for the accepted input and is never renewed by tool calls, context hooks or invalidation; locate, discovery, reads, loop decisions, check preparation and final validation all spend it, and so does any lane sharing the preparation lease. The finalization reserve is a fifth of the remainder, between 100 ms and 2000 ms (the real table measured 0.76–1.1 s of final validation). Cancellation, staleness and outer expiry still forbid publication. Total prescreen wall time, the configured allowance and its remainder at publication are telemetry fields; nothing about the wait is hidden.

**Telemetry.** Each loop decision records `loop_decision` with the chosen operation label or `finish`, the coverage and consistency choices and the offered count. The `prepared` event additionally carries `stop_reason`, `retrieval` (status, steps, rounds), the final `assessment`, the bounded per-round `choices`, a locate summary (batches, judged, unjudged, located, seeded, milliseconds) and a bounded `loop_trace` (at most 32 events), so "finished because sufficient" is distinguishable from "gave up" in the campaign telemetry. These records never feed back into a later turn.

Acceptance: two different requests over a graph whose relevant entities lie outside the current scene must receive different located orderings and first catalog pages; a state that fails the old single 32,768-byte bound but satisfies both documented limits must pack; a prepared note must carry `stop_reason`. Deterministic tests use controlled decision ports; Jev's real locate quality, latency and Keeper adoption remain live-provider and canonical-table gates.

### 124.11 Which binding keys void a prepared result, and which are re-checked per material (2026-09-24, live gate #5; amends §124.1, §124.6 and §135.6)

**Evidence.** Live gate #5 used campaign `gate5-haunting-0259`, turn 2, run `run-01a0d238-db4d-72e1-ae72-5c2b2105bb58`, read s1. The
prescreen spent 12 Jev calls in 6.8 s: the locate judged 277 cards, the loop took five steps and finished `sufficient`. The final
validation then discarded all of it as `binding_changed`, and the compile ran without material. The read began at 07:02:16.7Z and
the fallback came at 07:02:23.5Z. In that window the npc-voice lane submitted Arty Wilmot's voice (`voice.submit`,
`kernel-ts/voice/index.ts:55-57` → `kernel-ts/voice/jobs.ts:241` `campaign.writeWorld`, event `dossier-established` at
07:02:23Z). The lane had opened that job after turn 1. It wrote the package's dossier into `world.json`, and `world` is part of
`stateStamp`. The owner's check over the retained keys answered `current`, because those keys were graph units of four entities
and one rule clause, and they depend only on `source_revision` and `rules_revision`. The host then compared `stateStamp` itself
(`extensions/table/prescreen.ts:633-634` at `a575e01e6`) and threw the whole result away. Turn 1's journal and memory lanes had
already landed at 07:01:39Z and 07:01:41Z, before turn 2 started. So none of `memory_revision`, `npc_revision` or
`records_revision` moved. The npc-voice lane is not the only writer: any post-turn lane can land during the next turn's read.

**Run keys void the prepared result.** They are `campaign`, `worldline`, `loop`, `turn`, `source_revision`, `rules_revision`,
`scene` and `adapter`. A page (catalog or read) whose binding differs on one of them ends the preparation. So does the final
check. The preparation ends with `fallback: "binding_changed"` and `key` set to that key. A page also compares `catalog_revision`:
it is requested with the same query, so a change is a change of the owner's catalog.

**Volatile keys are re-checked per material.** They are `stateStamp`, `memory_revision`, `npc_revision` and `records_revision`.

- *Pages.* Every page of the loop is requested with the run keys and `catalog_revision` only, so the owner serves current state
  and a lane's write does not refuse the page. When a page's binding shows a volatile key different from the one the preparation
  bound, the host records the drift. It does not discard anything at that point.
- *Final check.* The final check is requested with the complete original binding, the retained workspace keys and the request's
  query (so the owner computes `catalog_revision` from the same query). The owner compares each key's dependencies (§124.1). A
  stale answer now also names `stale_keys`: the requested keys whose dependencies include a changed key. If every changed key is
  volatile, the host drops exactly those materials and publishes the rest. Each dropped material becomes a gap with
  `reason: "binding_changed"` and its ordinary read continuation. The Keeper sees the reason and the read. The changed key
  stays private: it is recorded in `details.prescreen.gap_details` and the `prepared` row's `pending_reads` as `key`, with
  several keys joined by `+`. A stale answer that names a run key, or that carries no `stale_keys`, voids the result as
  above.
- *Memory.* Memory materials answer to their own owner. A `refresh` from the memory finisher, whether in the loop or at the
  final check, drops the memory materials it covers with `key: "memory_revision"`. It no longer fails the preparation.
- *What §124.6 still forbids.* §124.6 says stale bindings prohibit publication. That now means: a stale material is never
  published, and a run key's change still publishes nothing. A volatile change removes the materials it reaches. It does not
  remove the packet: a packet whose every material was dropped still carries the gaps and their reads.
- *Bound.* The one final owner check is the re-check. There is no second check and no retry. A material read after a drift is
  still checked against the original binding, so a fresh read of a drifted dependency is dropped rather than trusted.
- *Legacy.* The legacy v1 read catalog has no per-key dependency view, so it keeps the full comparison, and a volatile change
  still voids it.

**Telemetry.**

- The `fallback` row carries `key`.
- The `prepared` row carries `binding_refresh: {changed, dropped}` when a volatile key changed during the run.
- The run's read row (§135.6) carries `fallback: "binding_changed"` with `key`.
- The read row's `jev_calls`, and the run's `jevCalls` budget, now count the calls of a prescreen that fell back. On gate #5 the
  read row said 0 while 12 had been spent. *(Amended 2026-09-24 by §135.6's SL-22 addendum: the read row still counts them, and the run's decision
  budget no longer does.)*

*Kernel.* `table.workspace.read` in `preselect` mode adds `stale_keys` to `materials.check` when `status` is `stale`, next to
`changed` and `keys`. A check without keys still compares every key, and its `stale_keys` is empty.

*Tests.* `tests/extension/prescreen-binding-drift.test.mjs` runs the real kernel on the Haunting's opening. The lane writes go
through their real RPCs:

- The gate #5 shape: a `voice.submit` lands before the finish decision. `stateStamp` changes, and the graph material
  publishes with `binding_refresh: {changed: ["stateStamp"], dropped: 0}`.
- A `voice.submit` lands before a later catalog page. The page is served and nothing is voided.
- A `voice.submit` lands after an investigator `look` was read. Only that current-state material is dropped, with the private
  key `stateStamp`, and the graph material stays.
- A `table.apply` move lands mid-run. The fallback names `scene`.
- The owner's `stale_keys`: a stateStamp change names the investigator key and not the graph unit, and a keyless check names
  none.
- On the hybrid engine, the run's read row carries `fallback: "binding_changed"` and `key: "scene"`, and its `jev_calls`
  equals the discarded prescreen's.

## 125. Shared foreground evidence and NPC preparation (#109)

Specification: [NPC reactions in shared Keeper preparation](specs/npc-prescreen-integration.md). This integration preserves sections 123 and 124's authority and background owners. Its acceptance follows the actual Keeper provider request and real player interaction, not callback counts.

### 125.1 One preparation owner, separate perspectives

The existing host context owner may claim automatic NPC preparation through the private preparation-owner event. A claimed session does not also run the old standalone before-agent-start NPC wait. The NPC bridge retains explicit evaluate and adds prepare/finalize: prepare returns an advisory result plus a host-only NPC revision checkpoint; finalize rereads current limited perspectives and removes stale results before final request assembly. Neither checkpoint nor the supplied decision port enters Keeper content. Without the integrated owner the existing standalone NPC path remains compatible.

The versioned workspace catalog may receive host-only npc_perspectives:true. It returns separate limited NPC views derived from the same authoritative world/graph/memory/record snapshot used for the catalog. This does not replace Keeper dossier material with a public view, or give an NPC the Keeper's private source context. The existing npc.perspectives read uses the same projection owner. Prepared views include canonical input/scope, availability, accepted personality/history and response-bank revision; source material relevance never establishes presence or perception.

### 125.2 Concurrent work with a single allowance and capacity owner

After mandatory baseline preparation, the accepted input has one absolute automatic deadline. Both enabled branches share at most the existing six-second material allowance; NPC-only uses its existing configured short allowance. NPC's shorter child deadline is inside the outer allowance, not added before it. Context repeats, tool results, retries and invalidation never reset the allowance. Completed independent work can reach finalization despite an unrelated child timeout; cancellation or stale binding cannot be converted to completion.

One shared-auth adapter provides the combined foreground concurrency limit. The preparation owner reserves and settles every dispatched decision once in its shared allowance and, when present, once in the canonical parent provider budget. Branch limits remain subdivisions; an exhausted owner never creates a new independent fallback. Background tool-enabled authors and canonical publication keep their existing owners and never consume a mandatory foreground authoring round.

### 125.3 Final handoff and compatibility

The final context projection budgets evidence and NPC advice together, without promoting an intention to fact or allowing duplicate promises to crowd out their original attribution. Early NPC results are rechecked after material preparation, because memory, presence, personality or response banks may change while another branch runs. The real converted provider payload supplies delivery evidence. Prepared, retained, delivered and used remain distinct outcomes.

Material preselection and NPC advice keep their independent enablement semantics. A dossier already supplied to the Keeper does not suppress an appropriate NPC response; a relevant absent person does not act remotely. The existing explicit response-evaluation read can reuse compatible results and retains its ordinary tool/task authority. No new public verb, perception parser, credential route or game mutation owner is introduced.

## 126. Prepare the current action without avoidable foreground work (2026-09-22)

The user authorized wiring and refactoring after the real #108 comparison failed to improve player waiting. This section extends sections 124 and 125: the objective is fewer unnecessary serial Keeper/provider stages while preserving source fidelity, player agency, kernel settlement and useful incomplete results. It does not authorize a different model, synthetic play, skipped admission, unreviewed success claims or removal of retained failures. Primary acceptance remains actual converted Keeper requests and canonical live player turns.

### 126.1 Demand-directed material selection and actual delivery

The v2 material catalogue must distinguish discoverable material from the bounded page returned in one read. Its continuation reaches the host and can be consumed under the same captured revision and preparation budget. A first-page cap is not a relevance judgment. The host reserves work for evaluating delivered coverage and, when necessary, one useful continuation/supplement; initial scanning must not routinely spend the entire decision allowance before that stage. Long sources remain bounded and explicit about unsearched ranges rather than becoming mandatory whole-book reads.

Recent actual read identities and retained results are available to material preparation whenever that feature is enabled, independently of the older workspace mode. A delivered ordinary tool result, conversation original or capsule projection is part of the real baseline; matching material must preserve attribution and any additional conditions rather than either duplicating the whole record or discarding a richer source merely because a label matches.

Selection and packing operate on source-owned material units with explicit required context/dependencies and size, not only whole entities. The host copies exact issued fields/ranges; it does not ask Jev to rewrite source prose or infer missing parameters. Necessary support for the declared action is packed before optional background. If a selected group cannot fit, use a smaller complete source-owned projection or represent its missing conditions explicitly; arbitrary string truncation cannot retain a sufficiency claim. Where independent relevance choices duplicate support, the dependent coverage pass sees the actual packed set before choosing additional units. Candidate scope, decisions, selected-but-omitted material and final delivery remain separately observable through bounded host-only identities and reasons.

### 126.2 Read-only check preparation in the normal Keeper path

When material preselection is enabled, the first eligible preparation for an accepted player input may read the existing `table.resolve.options` and prepare advisory check choices alongside other independent support. Reuse the existing ordinary-resolve policy through shared pure policy builders/validation; the broader TaskRuntime/plan-submission mode is not required and no parallel rule selector is introduced.

The result distinguishes `ordinary`, `no_roll`, `incumbent`, `needs_player` and `unknown`. An ordinary suggestion names only an issued current actor/profile/decision and bounded difficulty/modifier choices. The raw player declaration and established public context own action selection; a private clue, predicted NPC response or optional plan never grants authorization. Unsupported specialized families, missing profiles, NPC executors, pending choices and uncertain parameters retain their existing owner or remain unknown. A suggested future check is not a rolled result.

The host does not execute the suggested resolve. The Keeper may use or correct it and invokes the ordinary canonical tool; admission, Mod validation, arithmetic and transaction receipts remain in that existing path. No numerical result is predicted. Check advice carries private input/world/rules/profile bindings, is checked after parallel preparation and dropped if obsolete. It shares the existing preparation adapter, parent accounting, deadline and final request budget with evidence and NPC support. Optional check failure does not erase independently valid evidence. The public projection shows current semantic choices and unresolved needs, never private hashes, provider metadata or an assertion that a check already happened.

### 126.3 Foreground item identity and background enrichment

A requested item handover requires a real persistent identity, ownership and transaction receipt in this turn. Descriptive or usage enrichment that no current operation consumes must not automatically hold that transaction open. The implementation must separate those dependencies at the existing definition/object owners, retain unknown mechanics as unknown, and publish later enrichment through their revision/acceptance guards. It must not create a key-specific exception, infer ordinary status from an item-name list, turn absent mechanics into confirmed no-effects, or narrate an uncommitted handover.

Fields needed to execute a current weapon, spell, document, resource effect or requested usage remain mandatory before that execution. Ordinary read/move/ownership operations must not implicitly acquire execution authority from a partial definition. Existing accepted compatible definitions and usages are reused. Background work is bounded, durable under the existing job owner, and cannot overwrite an object whose relevant basis changed or race a newer accepted enrichment.

**Implementation decision: reuse existing inventory identity and queued adoption.** Do not invent an incomplete accepted definition or default unknown effects to an empty executable profile. A host-only `mods.identity.plan {campaign, define, object}` may prepare/reuse the existing create job and return eligibility, its existing job/provenance and a reason; it changes no game state and grants no handover authority. Eligibility is structural and tied to current operation dependencies: one ordinary `item` definition without a template and one investigator-bound identity transfer referring to it, with no same-batch execution, document, container, condition, weapon or spell dependency. Unsupported or ambiguous shapes retain the incumbent path. The transaction rechecks that eligibility and the existing giver/disposition/ownership rules rather than trusting a caller boolean.

An eligible queued definition plus transfer atomically creates an ordinary inventory identity with the actual quantity, giver and owner, a truthful transfer receipt and `pending_definition:true`, and a retained adoption request bound to that acquisition and its relevant basis. This is owned equipment whose executable definition is unprepared, not a complete managed instance or a fictitious completed creator. Other authorized clue/cash/move effects in the transaction may finish. Creator work continues through the existing tool-enabled job, validation and acceptance path. At a safe boundary, a ready result is promoted through the existing queued definition/adoption transaction; the original handover is never replayed. Until then execution-dependent operations refuse or request preparation explicitly.

An unfinished or failed optional creator must not be synchronously retried merely because `narrate`, an unrelated action or the next player input invokes queue reconciliation. Reconciliation publishes ready work and resumes eligible optional work in its background owner. A genuinely requested execution may join the existing job through the ordinary preparation gate. Removal, transfer, quantity/basis changes, cancellation, restart and same-name replacement must not let a late result resurrect or adopt a different acquisition; revalidation covers the claimed item, not unrelated world changes. Preserve failure evidence and a usable pending state. A complete player turn, including delivery, must remain unblocked while a test-held optional creator has not finished.

**0.9.5a merge note (2026-09-23).** §129.4 landed on the same day from the table-loop branch and defers *every*
`define` in any batch shape through a queued registration and a placeholder definition for the placement.
On 0.9.5a a define + placement batch therefore takes §129.4, not this section's optional-identity plan:
`deferOrdinaryIdentities` is no longer called from the apply hook (its `mods.identity.plan` operation and its
own tests remain until this section is retired or re-scoped to what §129.4 does not cover). The optional
creator bookkeeping in `mods.queued` and the safe-boundary resume are kept and run beside the turn (§129).

### 126.4 Audit submission matches the existing validated protocol

The observed live audit spent its only format repair on misplaced subreviews, then failed because a same-locus result supplied a locus where the existing protocol requires null. The private `submit_audit` tool schema and pinned instruction must express the same nesting and closed mode/field choices as the existing schema-2 validator. Required subreviews belong inside `continuity_review`; same-locus/transition null rules must be explicit. Host-owned source aliases remain references, not copied prose. Keep all reference, required-review, semantic finding and live-freshness checks; do not normalize a conflicting semantic judgment into pass, drop a required subreview, increase the repair allowance or treat unreviewed delivery as success. This is a producer/validator contract repair, not a new audit policy.

## 127. Lookup is honest about a module without an original document (2026-09-22)

Real table 2026-09-22 (installed App, built-in starter `the-haunting`, turn 1). The Keeper held four clue handles from the capsule (`knott-macario-summary`, `knott-keys`, …), passed them together as one `lookup kind=module` query and read `not_found`; it then asked `lookup kind=source source_mode=answer` and was refused with `fix: bind the matching original PDF with module.source.bind`. A built-in starter has no original document by construction, the Keeper cannot call `module.source.bind`, and an error's fix is executed literally.

### 127.1 Exact handles resolve, several at once

`table.lookup kind=module` first tries its whole `query` as it always did. When that query splits on whitespace or commas into two or more words and **every** word is exactly the handle or node id of a graph node (the same normalisation `search` already uses for exact keys), the result is those entities in the order given, deduplicated, at most 8 — a handle two nodes share (`knott-commission` is a clue and a quest) yields both, as it does when it is the whole query — filtered by `expected_kind` when supplied. This is identifier grammar, not semantic splitting: a query with any word that is not a handle is ordinary search text and is not partially matched, so free text is never cut into guessed handles.

### 127.2 A module without an original document refuses source reading with the working road
